This sale involved the transfer of a portfolio of 359 apartment complexes in the US and Germany totaling 87,667 units which were held by Archstone-Smith Trust at the time of merger with Tishman Speyer Real Estate Venture VII LP and Lehman Brothers Holdings Inc. This figure includes all properties and units under construction as of the date of closing. The majority of Archstone's holdings are concentrated in the Washington DC metropolitan area, Southern California, the San Francisco Bay area, the New York metropolitan area, Seattle and Boston. The transaction was valued at approximately $22,200,000,000 and included Archstone-Smith's outstanding debt. 

The merger was financed by Tishman Speyer, Lehman Brothers Holdings Inc, Banc of America Strategic Ventures Inc., Barclay's Capital and affiliates. Additional funding was provided by Fannie Mae, which purchased a $7.1 billion credit facility secured by 105 existing multifamilty properties that were part of the transaction.  Concurrently, Freddie Mac executed a $1.8 billion structured transaction that will provide new financing for 32 properties and approved assumption of an additional 15 properties.

Preliminary discussions regarding the merger were begun during the week of April 16,2007. A press release was released on the 29th of May, 2007 announcing the execution of the merger agreement. A memorandum of understanding was reached on the 17th of August with several discordant shareholders who opposed the merger and stockholder approval was granted on August 21,2007. The merger became effective on October 5, 2007.  In addition to the real property transfer, each common share of Archstone-Smith Trust was converted into $60.75 in cash per share.

Morgan Stanley was retained by the Board of Trustees of Archstone Smith to act as its financial advisor. Hogan & Hartson acted as legal counsel. Hogan & Hartson, Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz, legal counsel to Tishman Speyer and Weil, Gotshal & Manges LLP, legal counsel to Lehman Brothers, negotiated the terms of the merger agreement.

The Irvine Company subsequently offered (contingent upon the successful closing of the merger) to acquire, for an estimated $1.4 billion, a 90% interest in 16 apartment communities located throughout Orange and San Diego counties in Southern California. 

Barclays and Bank of America own 54% while Lehman Brothers Holdings owns 47%. (Comp note updated on 12.5.11)

HOUSTON, TX – The Houston office of HFF (Holliday Fenoglio Fowler, L.P.) announced today that it closed the sale of James Plaza, a 42,788-square-foot office building in Houston.
HFF senior managing director Dan Miller and associate director Marty Hogan led the investment sales team on behalf of the seller, BGK Group. 3934 FM 1960, L.P., affiliated with Boxer Property of Houston, purchased the asset for an undisclosed amount free and clear of debt.

notes.value:
Texas is a nondisclosure state and typically there is no information available regarding the sale price. Yet for this sale, the price was provided by a source deemed reliable. 

The reliable source was contacted and reported the 232 unit facility sold for $9.1 million on 10/29/2009. Under contract for 60 days, the closing went smoothly with no setbacks. The deal was negotiated off market as the buyer and seller had been involved in previous deals. The property was significantly damaged from Hurricane Ike, but the source would not elaborate on what specifically was damaged nor provide the cost of damages. Roof repairs were done prior to the closing, but the buyer is responsible for remediation of all other issues going forward. The source was under the assumption this was the upleg of a 1031 exchange for the buyer, but could not say so definitively. Supposedly the seller's motivation of disposition was that the buyer's offer was too good to pass up and it was just time to sell the asset. The buyer assumed a Freddie Mac loan in the deal. Income/expense information was not disclosed and no other details were provided.

When the transfer documents become available they will attached to this report.
This is a bonafide gift and the grantor received nothing in return, R&T 11911.

TA Associates Realty, on behalf of The Realty Associates Fund VII LP has sold Legacy Park Apartments to Adams LaSalle Realty for an undisclosed price, reflecting a Cap Rate of 7.12%.  The apartment complex is comprised of thirteen buildings all of which are three-stories. The fourteenth building is used for the clubhouse. There are 304 units in total and are divided into one and two bedroom apartments.  The property was built in 1994 and totals 260,397 sq ft, which is situated on 13.43 acres.  

TA Associates Realty owned the property for four years prior to selling and during that period renovated the exterior of the complex.  At the time of sale 92% of Legacy Park was occupied.

The sellers motivation to sale was a weakness in the property market and to diversify the funds assets.  The buyer is looking to take advantage of the weak market by purchasing 2,000 to 3,000 units in 2010.  

A loan for just under $12 million was taken out by the purchaser from Freddie Mac.

The seller was represented by Hendricks & Partners and purchaser was unrepresented.

The buyer's SEC filing reports this acquisition was part of a 4 property purchase for   $154 million.  The individual sales prices were not released.  This property has 678 units.

For related acquisitions refer to CoStar Comps IDs 1857668, 1843222, and 1862211.

The apartment complex reported the unit mix, there are 42 studio, 276 one-bedroom, 72 one-bedroom one bath, 252 two-bedroom two bath, and 36 three-bedroom three bath.

notes.value:
The listing broker and seller verified the 165 apartments and 38,543 SF of retail space sold for $31.1 million.  

The property is a historical site and is eligible for historical tax credits.  

The property was placed on the market 6/30/10, and went under contract 9/27/10.

The apartments were 93% occupied at closing. The retail space had a 12,000 SF space that was vacant but rent was still being paid by the former tenant, Rite Aide. The rest of the retail space was 80% occupied. The property was marketed with an in-place NOI of $2,100,522. The actual cap rate was verified as 6.75%.  the seller reported the cap rate was high, however did not release a cap rate or financial information.

The property was built in 1911 and 1912, and fully renovated in 2004.  The property is not subject to rent control, however 33 of the units are designated low income.  

There are 22 subterranean parking spaces.  In addition, the property has a long term lease for 140 spaces in a Maple Street parking structure, which includes shuttle service.  Per the marketing brochure: " The remainder of the parking for Santee Court is provided at a parking structure located at 636 S Maple Street, approximately one block away from the subject property. The structure at 636 S. Maple is owned by the Metropolitan Transit Authority. Santee Court leases 140 spaces from this parking structure for the exclusive use of the residents of the property on a long term basis. The lease term expires in approximately 60 years."

The seller originally was going to exit the property by converting the apartments to condominiums.  That was no longer feasible in this economic market.  The loan was maturing on the property and the seller did not want to refinance, so they decided to sell the property.  The buyer felt this property was a good opportunity to buy with a discount to replacement cost.

Santee Court possesses a vesting condominium tract map-tract number 53871.

The sale date was 10/29/10, the deed recorded on 11/1/10.

The source stated that there was nothing atypical that affected the price of the asset, but did state that the property was distressed, and thus the sale was too. 

It was stated that the buyer plans to occupy three floors initially, and maybe additional space in the future.  They own an adjacent property, and location-wise, the property made a lot of sense for the buyer.  

It was also stated that there is significant deferred maintenance to the property, including roof repair/replacement, chillers, elevators, etc.  A dollar figure was not given, but the source indicated a lot of money will be spent on that maintenance.  

The seller acquired the property in the late 2000s as a sale leaseback, and the tenant went bankrupt and vacated the majority of the space.  As this property is outside the seller's typical profile, it was stated that they thought it best to sell the property.  

Expenses were only $7.50/SF, but that figure was not grossed up and reflected the low occupancy.  Grossed up expenses were likely to be around $9.50/SF.

Per the attached SEC filing Lehman Brothers Holdings Inc. closed on the purchase of a $1.325 billion stake in real estate group Archstone, raising its total stake in the sought-after apartment company to 73.5%. 

Lehman Brothers held a 47% ownership interest in Archstone prior to this transaction.  There was a purchase agreement entered into between the sellers and Equity Residential for this 26.5% stake in Archstone prompting Lehman Brothers to exercise their right of first offer and move forward with this acquisition.  This sale was of one half of the interest held by the sellers who still hold an additional 26.5% interest in Archstone.

It is reported by Archstone that as of September 30, 2011 they had an ownership interest in a total of 428 apartment communities in the United States and Europe which include 73,955 units.  They have an ownership interest in 179 communities in the United States alone which include 60,136 units.  These figures include communities that were under construction.

As of March 31, 2012 Archstone reported a gross income of $273.616 million and a net operating income of $180.242 million.  By using 26.5% of those figures a roughly estimated cap rate for the transaction would be 3.60% and the gross rent multiplier would be 18.27.  The motivation behind Lehman's acquisition was to move forward with their strategy to take Archstone public.

This transaction and the properties included are still being researched.

Reportedly, Lehman Brothers Holdings Inc. closed on the purchase of a $1.58 billion stake in real estate group Archstone, raising its total stake in the sought-after apartment company to 100%. 

Lehman Brothers held a 73.5% ownership interest in Archstone prior to this transaction.  There was a purchase agreement entered into between the sellers and Equity Residential for this 26.5% stake in Archstone prompting Lehman Brothers to exercise their right of first offer and move forward with this acquisition.  This sale was the remaining interest held by the sellers.  

The sellers are required to pay $80 million to Equity Residential as a break-up fee.  The buyer is paying an additional $70 million, not included in the sale price, to Equity Residential as a termination fee.

It is reported by Archstone that as of March 31, 2012 they had an ownership interest in a total of 434 apartment communities in the United States and Europe which include 73,135 units.  They have an ownership interest in 190 communities in the United States alone which include 61,126 units.  These figures include communities that were under construction.  There are some communities in which Archstone holds a small minority interest in that were not attached to this report.

As of March 31, 2012 Archstone reported a gross income of $273.616 million and a net operating income of $180.242 million.  By using 26.5% of those figures a roughly estimated cap rate for the transaction would be 3.02% and the gross rent multiplier would be 21.79.  The motivation behind Lehman's acquisition was to move forward with their strategy to take Archstone public.

It is assumed that there will not be documents recorded for this transaction as this is the sale of a portion of the underlying interest in Archstone who continues to own the properties.

The overall occupancy level for the portfolio was reported to be in the high seventies at the time of sale; therefore, a cap rate was not-applicable.

It was reported that several properties needed rehab work that included roofs, some down units, foundation issues, wood rot, exterior painting and parking lot work; therefore, there was a gambit of work needed on most of the properties, since they had been neglected through the foreclosure process.

The portfolio was owned by a group led by Goldarch Properties, which is led by Allen Gross, who also heads GFI Capital Resources of New York. Its eight properties were considered class B when the debt against them was securitized. After the Goldarch group purchased them, it re-branded them CityView. The properties were constructed during the late 1970s and early 1980s and were nearly 91% occupied through 2006.

After Hurricane Ike hit Houston in 2008, the performance of some of the properties, which are in the Greenspoint area of North Houston, suffered. And in early 2010, the CMBS loan was transferred to C-III Asset Management, the transaction's special servicer, because it was expected to default. C-II took over the portfolio through a foreclosure in June 2011.

The motivation for the seller was an REO sale.

The motivation for the buyer was to purchase Class C properties, complete a value-add opportunity by upgrading the units and selling them as part of their strategy.

Under the ground lease the duration of the interest extends until February 15, 2064 (55 years) and has four 10-year renewal options.

This transaction represents the sale of 2929 Briarpark Dr Houston, TX. This 139,443 square-foot office property sold for approximately $18,500,000 on December 20, 2012. Sources deemed reliable were able to report the sale price and other details of the transaction.

The property was about 95 percent leased and 90 percent physically occupied at the time of sale. The asset traded at about an eight percent cap rate. The $18,500,000 price reflects the gross purchase price. Credits were given to the buyer to bring the property up to city standards for the sprinkler system. The seller paid for half of the buildings new sprinklers and half of a new chilller. The seller paid for tenant improvements for a new lease and there was some deferred maintenance in the garage.

Equity Residential and AvalonBay Communities acquired Archstone on February 27, 2013 for a total price of about $15.65 billion.  This report represents the wholly owned properties being sold to Equity Residential.

Equity Residential is acquiring about 60% interest in Archstone which includes 100% ownership interest in 71 wholly-owned apartment communities with 20,160 units, a partial interest in an additional 2 properties with 768 units, 3 master leased properties with 853 units, and four communities under construction with 964 units.  In addition, they acquired fourteen land sites which when developed would contain a total of 4,318 units.

Equity Residential's portion of the purchase price totals about $8,755,212,760, exclusive of the joint venture acquisition.  The purchase price was funded through the issuance of 34,468,085 common shares of Equity Residential stock, which as of the close of business on February 26, 2013 was $56 per share, the assumption of $2.8 billion in existing debt, $1.675 billion in cash of which $1.1 billion was from the sale of non-core assets, $1.6 billion from the company's revolving credit facility and $750 million from bank term debt.

The cap rate for the transaction was updated in this report on March 7, 2013 from 4.7% from the original public filing at the time of contract to 4.5%.  The updated cap rate is based on the post-closing 8-K filing attached to this report showing the net operating income for the portfolio as of December 31, 2012 was $394,218,886.

The leasehold interest was acquired for 9 of the properties, the 2013 combined ground rent is $5,364,230.

Morrison Foerster's Washington D.C. corporate and securities partner, David Slotkin, and Los Angeles real estate partner, Thomas Fileti, represented Equity Residential in the acquisition.

See COMPS id 2688252 for more information regarding the joint venture acquisition by Equity Residential and AvalonBay Communities for the remaining assets of Archstone.  The joint venture assets include 14,000 apartment units located in Germany, six properties located in the United States and various development pursuit deals.

See COMPS id 2687922 for additional information regarding AvalonBay Communities acquisition of 66 apartment communities with 22,222 units of which 6 communities are under construction, an interest in 10 communities containing 2,040 units in which they will be general partner or managing member one of which is under construction, and three parcels of land which when developed would contain a total of 968 apartment units.  AvalonBay Communities portion of the purchase price totals about $6,520,922,809 as of the date of the purchase agreement.

The properties and assessment information are continuing to be added to this report.  Redwood Shores and Harborside in Redwood City, California are two phases of the same project and are listed under one property id in CoStar.

Equity Residential and AvalonBay Communities acquired Archstone on February 27, 2013 for a total price of about $15.69 billion.  This report shows the properties being sold to AvalonBay Communities.

AvalonBay acquired a roughly 40% interest in Archstone which includes 100% ownership interest in 60 apartment communities with 20,089 units of which 5 communities are under construction and will contain 1,198 units, an interest in 12 communities containing 2,851 units in which they will be general partner or managing member, and five parcels of land which when developed would contain a total of 1,414 apartment units.

In addition, the buyer lists Archstone Santa Clarita, a 157 unit under construction community, on their list of properties to be acquired but have not included the property in the count above.  The reason for the omission is unknown, although they acquired a 21.6% interest in Archstone Santa Clarita.

The number of properties attached to this report varies slightly due to the way the buyer counts the number of communities versus the way they are tracked in CoStar records. There are some communites that are in the process of being expanded that have 2 property records in CoStar during the construction process.  There is a land record created for the purpose of representing the additional air rights that traded for Kips Bay in New York.

AvalonBay Communities portion of the purchase price totals about $6,482,209,574 as of the date of the purchase agreement, including $400 million which is the portion of the purchase price allocated to the joint venture interest with Equity Residential.

The purchase price consists of $669 million to be paid in cash, the issuance of 14,889,706 shares of AvalonBay common stock valued at $125.94 per share as of closing on February 27, 2013 and the assumption of $3.938 billion in debt.

The cap rate was calculated based on the buyer's public filing at the time of contract.  The annualized net operating income for the original portfolio, which included 5 additional properties that have subsequently sold, was $303,157,570.  The net operating income divided by the original purchase price of $6,498,942,000, exclusive of the joint venture purchase price, equals 4.67%.  The price for the stabilized properties was $6,140,323,000 which would equate to a cap rate of 4.94% if examined exclusive of the additional properties acquired.

See COMPS id 2688252 for more information regarding the joint venture acquisition by Equity Residential and AvalonBay Communities for the remaining assets of Archstone for a purchase price of $814.3 million.

See COMPS id 2687917 for additional information regarding Equity Residential's acquisition of 71 wholly-owned apartment communities with 20,160 units, a partial interest in an additional 2 properties with 768 units, 3 master leased properties with 853 units, and four communities under construction with 964 units.  In addition, they acquired 14 land sites which when developed would contain a total of 4,318 units.  Equity Residential's portion of the purchase price totals $8,755,212,760 exclusive of the joint venture acquisition.

The sale includes Galleria Plaza I & II, two office buildings located at 5251 & 5333 Westheimer Road.  It also includes the adjacent retail properties, Sage Plaza at 2610 - 2680 Sage Road, the 8,800 square foot retail building at 5250 W Alabama Street, and the 3,892 square foot Regions Bank building located at 5251 Westheimer Road.

The 217,005 square foot Galleria Plaza I is also known as TeleCheck Plaza.  The 11-story office building was fully leased at the time of sale. The sale includes a 49 unit loft property located at 818 S Grand Ave. in the heart of South Park district of downtown Los Angeles. Representing the best of urban loft living, the property is situated within easy walking distance to Staples Center, LA Live, Downtown Restaurant Row, and the Walt Disney Music Center. The property is surrounded by museums, restaurants, shopping, theaters and exciting nightlife that exists in downtown Los Angeles. With the new Empire Hotel going in across the street, the Downtown Streetcar project fully funded and Carmel Partners 700 unit project in construction across the street to the north, South Park lofts is surrounded by over a billion dollars of new development.

In 2004, the California Historic Resources Commission granted the property historic landmark status, and shortly thereafter, the property was also listed on the National Register of Historic Places. While the outside of the building retains its historic importance, the interior of the high-end lofts provides many features today's renters are actively looking for including exposed brick walls, polished concrete floors and high end condo grade kitchens and bathrooms. In addition, the property provides a huge rooftop garden with a spa, grilling area, glass enclosed rooftop gym for residents and an onsite cafe at the street level. South Park Lofts has a concierge service provided by Polaris Property Management that delivers convenience and flexibility for both apartment residents and small business owners.

The motivation for the seller was an REO sale.

The motivation for the buyer was to expand their firm's portfolio to include another asset in the lively downtown Los Angeles community. This is the second acquisition in the downtown area for them, and the tenth major acquisition in Los Angeles in three years.

Around 9/9/2013, the joint venture between Crescent Real Estate Equities and Barclays Capital sold the office properties commonly known as the Greenway Plaza and 777 Main to Cousins Properties Inc. for $1,110,000,000 or, approximately $208 per square foot.

The subject properties are located at 777 Main Street in Fort Worth, Texas and along Greenway Plaza in Houston, Texas.  Greenway Plaza was 92% occupied and 777 Main was 94% occupied at the time of sale.

The buyer has described the acquisition of these trophy assets as opportunistic and value-add driven while still maintaining a strong balance sheet poised for growth.  This is the up-leg on a 1031 exchange for the buyer.

The expected first year cap rate is 7.4% based on the contractual rents only, however expectations are increases in below market rents and lease-up of vacant space with a price that is well under replacement cost.

For Greenway Plaza the average remaining lease term is 6.4 years with rents ~19% below market. The sales price was confirmed by one of the brokers, and the buyers' press release. The subject property was listed on the market at $21.5 million, and sold for that amount. The property is located at the corner of Hilgard and Le Conte, immediately adjacent to the University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA) in the upscale neighborhood of Westwood, one of the strongest multifamily submarkets in Los Angeles. The property is a four-story complex with gated two-level subterranean parking garage. The property features a mix of one-bedroom, one-bedroom and den and two-bedroom units along with some two-story townhouse style units. Majority of the units have fireplaces and balconies.

The cap rate was reported at 3.66%. The property was fully leased at the time of sale. The property contains no sales conditions that would have affected the sales price, and contains no deferred maintenance.

The buyers plan to undertake an extensive capital improvement program to reposition the vintage building into one of the area's premier student oriented housing communities with upgrades to both the interior and exterior of the building. The capital improvement program includes upgrades to the building systems, modernizing the interior and introducing technology to make it more functional and appealing to the international student population at UCLA. Some of the specific upgrades include a fully equipped gym, kitchens and bathrooms upgrades, installing washers and dryers in each unit and a rooftop lounge with a sun deck, barbecue and fire pit.

The buyers are rebranding the property as 888 Hilgard, and have retained feng shui consultant David Cho as well as designer James Rosen, who has renovated several properties in the area. 

The motivation for the buyers was a very well designed and constructed building located at a great location in Westwood.

Essex Property Trust entered into a definitive agreement to acquire BRE Properties at a transaction valued at $56.21 per BRE share as of December 18, 2013.  The original agreement was for Essex to pay BRE shareholders $12.33 per share in cash and issue 0.2971 share of Essex stock.  

As of December 31, 2013, BRE Properties owned 73 multi-family properties including 20,724 units and had a joint venture interest in one additional community with 252 units (JV property: 800 West Queen Creek Road, Chandler, AZ).  In addition, they owned six communities in California which were in various stages of construction and development totaling 1,888 units.

The total transaction value, which includes the joint venture formations that closed on March 31, 2014 and secured and unsecured debt assumed, was confirmed to be $6,848,422,000 as of the date of sale.  The breakdown of the purchase price calculation and the price allocation between the transactions are below.

Prior to the closing of this transaction, on March 31, 2014 BRE Properties sold a 50% interest in 17 properties to joint venture partners in 3 transactions.  The combined sale price was $888 million of which $475 million was financed.  As a result of this sale, BRE made a special distribution to shareholders of $5.15 per share.  This reduced the cash paid per share by Essex to $7.18 per share.  See CoStar COMPS id 2994374 and 3020959 for additional information regarding the joint venture transactions.

According to a party to the transaction there were 77.4 million outstanding shares of BRE stock along with preferred shares that had been redeemed for $54 million. 

As of the close of business April 1, 2014, Essex Property Trust stock price was $174.00 per share.  *The sale price and cap rate for this transaction were updated to reflect the value of Essex stock as of April 1st along with the total of secured and unsecured debt assumed.  

The 77.4 million outstanding shares at $51.70 (0.2971 of $174.00) equals $4,001,580,000 in stock issuance.  The cash paid in the amount of $7.18 per BRE share equals $555,732,000.  The special distribution paid to stockholders the day before closing due to the joint venture formations is valued at $398,610,000.  The contact confirmed that the amount of total debt assumed in the transaction was $1,838,500,000 plus $54 million for the redeemed preferred shares.  This totals $6,848,422,000 less the $888 million sale price for the joint venture sales on March 31st results in an approximate price of $5,960,422,000 for this transaction.  The purchase price for this transaction was reduced by the full price of the joint venture transactions as it is assumed that the $475 million in new financing by the joint venture resulted in a similar reduction in existing debt by BRE.

The 10-K filed by BRE for the year ending 2013 reports a net operating income of $288.987 million, less general and administrative expenses of $23.037 million results in net income of $265.95 millon.  The cap rate was calculated to be 3.88% using the total transaction value as the net income includes the ownership interest conveyed to the joint venture owners.

BRE reports a total asset value of $3,626,525,000, which includes ($879,640,000) in accumulated depreciation.  As of September 30, 2013 BRE had mortgage debt totaling $711,527,000 at a weighted average rate of 5.6%.

Eastdil Secured brokered the transaction.  Essex Property Trust was advised by Dean Pappas and Gilbert Manna of Goodwin Proctor, LLP.

The sales price was confirmed by one of the brokers. The subject property was only 50% leased at the time of sale due to the seller knew the property needed major renovations. Since the property was under rent controlled, when tenants previously vacated, the seller did not lease the units on purpose, so that it would be easier for the buyer of the property to get the property completely vacant in order to complete a total rehab of the property. The property needed massive rehab work that included roof replacement, plumbing work, redo of the lobby, exterior work and other work estimated at several millions. The buyer's renovation program will include interior and common area improvements, new building systems and amenities including a rooftop lounge with unobstructed views of the iconic Hollywood Sing. All the renovation will be done while remaining true to the property's rich architectural integrity and historic charm. The renovation program is expected to be completed in 2015.

The property was built in 1926 for the widow of silent film pioneer Thomas Ince as a residential apartment house for Hollywood notables. The classic Hollywood Spanish Colonial style building was designed by Arthur E. Harvey. The property was designated a Los Angeles Historic Cultural Monument in 1986.

The 50-unit building features a mix of studio and one-bedroom apartments ranging in size from 505 SF to 706 SF. The property also includes two, 1,214 SF two-bedroom, two-bath townhomes. Each unit features original hardwood floors, vaulted ceilings with stenciled wood beams, ornate crown moldings, wrought iron balconies and classic cabinetry and plumbing.

The motivation for the seller was they had owned the property for more than fifty years, and thought it was a good time to sell due to market timing.

The motivation for the buyer was a great location at the base of Hollywood Hills to complete a value-add opportunity through a complete renovation of the property. They think it is an irreplaceable asset that has been untouched for the past 50 years. They will reposition the property as luxury long-term rentals appealing to individuals seeking an authentic. The property will also feature a number of fully furnished , extended stay apartments catering to the executive engaged in the entertainment, Internet and technology business traveling to Hollywood to work on a project.

CenterPoint Properties has acquired a 27-building transportation advantaged portfolio in Houston, Texas. The properties are located within nine business parks, and total 3.6 Million square feet, also included in the sale over 10 acres of developable land. The aggregate occupancy was approximately 95% at the time the portfolio traded.

This was an opportunity for the buyer to acquire a port-proximate, predominately rail-served building portfolio, directly adjacent to substantial rail infrastructure. 

The majority of the facilities acquired are situated east of the Houston Central Business District. The buildings offer access to shipping channels including, the Union Pacific (UP) Settegast, UP Englewood and Burlington Northern Santa Fe Mykawa yards, the Port of Houston, and close proximity to a petrochemical refining complex.

The central location in relation to multiple modes of transportation provides tenants with decreased transportation-related expenses. The majority of the facilities acquired are designed for floor-stacked products with high turn ratios, which is a building feature in great demand in the Houston market. 

The property manager is now with Centerpoint Properties and will continue to manage the portfolio. The deal was under contract three to four months with no conditions disclosed. For the purpose of this report a escrow time of 105 days will be utilized.

A private fund affiliated with Dallas-based Crow Holdings acquired a 27-building, 2.35 million square foot industrial portfolio located in the Dallas-Fort Worth area and Houston, TX for an undisclosed amount. The eight Dallas-Fort Worth properties are located in the DFW Airport North, Great Southwest, Valwood and West Brookhollow industrial markets. The 11 buildings are 98.1 percent leased and total 1.015 million square feet. The eight Houston facilities are located in the Northwest and Southwest industrial markets and total 16 buildings with 1.335 million square feet. The deal closed in all cash but the buyer is currently working with HFF to secure debt to finance the acquisition.

The seller was a partnership between Mayfield Properties and AllianceBernstein, LP.

The HFF Dallas and Houston Investment Sales team represented the seller and procured the buyer in the transaction.

The sales price was confirmed by a reliable source. The subject property was 80% leased at the time of sale. The property was reported to total 407,915 SF by two sources, and 403,287 SF by one source. Our thoughts was it got remeasured, and we went with the 407,915 SF. The in-place cap rate was reported at 4.3%; therefore, we were able to calculate the NOI. The pro forma cap rate was reported at 6.5%. The total operating expenses was reported at $14/SF. The property contains no sales conditions that would have affected the sales price, and contains no deferred maintenance.

The property, which backs $53 million of debt that is securitized through Morgan Stanley Capital I, 2011-C3, was purchased from a venture led by Legacy Partners. The loan pays a 5.382% coupon and matures in August 2016. The property also supports $12 million of mezzanine financing held by Pearlmark Mezzanine Realty partners II and an affiliate of Salient Partners that pays a 9% coupon. 

The property is a 22-story Class A office tower of high quality office space and parking for 950 cars in a six-level garage and nearby surface lot. The building is well-positioned to benefit from the resurgence of development activity occurring in the Miracle Mile and Fairfax Commercial Districts, which include several new residential projects, the multi-million dollar renovation of the Peterson Automotive Museum, the new Academy of Motion Pictures Museum and the extension of the Purple Line of the Los Angeles Metro System. The new owners are planning significant additional investment into the property to elevate the building's position as a premier Westside office location.

The property's central location in close proximity to Beverly Hills, Hollywood and the resurgent Fairfax and West 3rd Street commercial corridors is a major attraction of the acquisition. The property's central location, awesome views, ample parking, large floor plates and lower cost structure make it a very compelling business location for entertainment, media, advertising and other creative companies as well as the firms servicing these users. Moreover, the planned expansion of the LA Metro will provide a critical public transportation link from 6300 Wilshire to the rest of the Los Angeles basin and will be a game-changer by improving the commute experience, an increasing factor in attracting and retaining employees.

The motivation for the seller was the end of their hold period.

The motivation for the buyer was a Class A asset at a great basis point. The acquisition represents a significant addition to their West Coast portfolio. They see tremendous opportunity for value creation in the Los Angeles basin and plan to continue their aggressive acquisition activity in the region. They are excited to continue to build on their relationship together, since the two firms share similar views about the long-term prospects of the market and are very compatible in terms of the skills each bring to their partnership.

Located between Koreatown and downtown, this is an area that is starting to see a tremendous amount of capital moving into it with several high rises and office-to-apartment conversions planned , along with East Coast investors trading into Los Angeles in an effort to find value. The pair were built between 1969 and 1976, has four passenger elevators between the two and according to CoStar data had a total of 249,011 SF being marketed (or 63% of the total space). Not all that space is economically or physically vacant, with 31,047 SF being sublet space and another 29,781 SF becoming vacant between September and December 2015. Adjusting for that, the actual vacant space was an estimated 188,183 SF, or 52.42% occupancy according to CoStar data.

The asset is located next to the Galleria Mall, the 2.4 million SF mall that is Texas' largest shopping center, draws about 30 million visitors per year and owned by Simon Property Group.

LPC believes the Galleria to be as good a location for office as one can get in Houston, and sees just upside for this submarket, and this asset specifically once the new hotels come online.

The seller was a partnership between Atlanta-based Songy Highroads, LLC and private equity giant The Carlyle Group. As referenced above, the partnership acquired the asset in 2013 (comp ID 2704743). The partnership was of the view that this was a good market to sell into, and having completed the capex program on the asset, to instead reallocate proceeds to the two-hotel development on this site.

These 14 properties, totaling 3,539 units were sold in a portfolio transaction. They were marketed as part of a portfolio of 22 properties in Texas as well as two in Georgia and one in Cincinnati that totaled 6,653 units.

The sale is a portfolio of four Class A office buildings totaling 1,725,000 SF located in Westwood, CA, a premier West Los Angeles submarket. The buyer is a joint venture between Douglas Emmett, Inc. and Qatar Investment Authority. Douglas Emmett plans to retain 20% to 30% of the equity in the joint venture, with the remaining interest being held by institutional partners. The joint venture has obtained a non-recourse $580 million interest-only loan with a seven-year term from Wells Fargo Bank. The interest rate is floating at Libor plus 1.40%., which as been fixed at 2.37% for five years through an interest rate swap. In accordance with generally accepted accounting principles, this joint venture will be consolidated in the financial statements of Douglas Emmett, Inc.

The motivation for the seller was the end of the fund's life.

The motivation for the buyer was a good fit for their current portfolio. With the addition of this portfolio, Douglas Emmett controls 74% of the Westwood Wilshire office corridor. Douglas Emmett's total commercial portfolio now consists of 66 office property totaling approximately 17.2 million rentable SF. Douglas Emmett also owns ten premier apartment communities in Los Angeles and Honolulu with a total of 3,336 units.

For QIA, this joint venture represents another step in its plans to significantly expand its US Investment portfolio, and follows other large investments in real estate such as in New York City last year. IN 2015, QIA announced plans to vest $35 billion in North America over five years.

The newly expanded Metro Expo Line is one-half mile away and within a five-mile radius there is more than 80,000,000 SF of office space. Considered to be at the epicenter of Los Angeles's high-tech business community, the Westside area currently has more than 1,000 startup businesses. 

The motivation for the buyer is a market-rate multifamily asset with a value-add component in a market with solid core demographics and excellent demand drivers. The property is positioned to experience sustained and consistent rent growth over the coming market cycle. Moreover they continue to build a long-term portfolio of small, value-add deals in A quality locations in Los Angeles. The sale is comprised of the historic San Fernando building that was converting from office to multifamily and ground floor retail located at 400 S Main St. in Los Angeles. The subject property sold for $37,135,000 or $530,500 per unit that includes a credit of $325,000 for painting, and for the Mills Act, since the property was a historic building. The multifamily portion was approximately 95% leased, and the approximately 11,500 SF of ground floor retail space was fully leased at the time of sale. The property contains deferred maintenance.

The in-place cap rate was reported at 2.32%; therefore, we were able to calculate the NOI. The cap rate was so low due to mainly below market rents. The pro forma cap rate was reported at 5.5%.

Originally built in 1907 as one of the city's most coveted office buildings, the 89,793 SF building was converted in 2000 to accommodate 70 large, loft-style multifamily units in addition to approximately 11,500 SF of ground floor retail and restaurant space.

The nine-story San Fernando Building is located next to some of the city's most notable buildings including the Hellman Building, Continental Building and Farmers & Merchants National Bank, the Old Bank District's namesake. The property earned a place in the National Register of Historical Place in 1986, prior to its conversion to loft and retail space, and has since been declared a Historic-Cultural Monument by the city of Los Angeles. The building also serves as a filming location, featured in scenes from Bull Durham and 500 Days of Summer among other notable films.

The motivation for the seller was partnership dissolution, and redeploy capital.

The motivation for the buyer was specialist in urban historic buildings to add to their portfolio.

Due to the below market occupancy of the property, it was acquired using a new secured, non-recourse $90 million interest only loan that matures in July 2019. Douglas Emmett's total office portfolio now consists of 67 office properties totaling approximately 17.6 million SF. Douglas Emmett also owns ten premier apartment communities in Los Angeles and Honolulu.

For QIA, this joint venture represents another step in its plans to significantly expand its US investment portfolio, and follows other large investments in real estate such as Manhattan west project in New York City last year and the acquisition of the Westwood Office portfolio in Los Angeles earlier this year with Douglas Emmett as its partner. notes.value:
The sales price was confirmed by one of the brokers. The sale is comprised of the Park Wilshire Apartments totaling 170 units located at 2424 Wilshire Blvd. in Los Angeles, CA. The sales price was reported at $27.4 million that equates to $161,176 per units. The subject property was not listed on the market for sale; therefore, the sale was an off-market transaction. The in-place cap rate was reported at 4%; therefore, we were able to calculate the NOI. The property contains no sales conditions that would have affected the sales price, and contains no deferred maintenance.

Designated as an Historic-Cultural Monument by the L.A. Cultural Heritage Commission, the Park Wilshire was designed by the famed architectural team of Clarence H. Russell and Norman W. Alpaugh. The eight story building is a beautiful example of the Italian Renaissance Revival style. Clad in polychrome red brick, the Park Wilshire originally opened in 1924 as a residential hotel. Today, the building features spacious studio, one bedroom and two bedroom apartments, many of which boast expansive city views. 

Location also favors the Park Wilshire Apartments. There are numerous restaurants, schools and shopping locations within walking distance, and Downtown and USC are only a short commute away. CoStar projects that redevelopment in the Downtown, Koreatown and Westlake submarkets will total eight billion dollars. 

The motivation for the seller was the end of their hold period. This was their downleg in a 1031 exchange.

The motivation for the buyer was a value-add opportunity through a renovation program as well as they own other properties in the area; therefore, this acquisition was a compliment to their existing portfolio. They will restore the original vitality and grandeur to the Park Wilshire, just as it has done in the renovation of its previous acquisitions of historic buildings. Prioritize in the renovation will be the restoration of the building's signature rooftop sign that had been an iconic fixture on Wilshire Blvd. since the 1920s. They will substantially upgrade the building with a refurbished lobby, new corridors, reconstructed and redesigned interiors, fresh landscaping and a brand new, fully-equipped, state-of-the-art fitness center and business center - all while maintaining the unique character and historic charm of the property. With the imminent completion of their renovations to the Wilshire Royale, located across the street, they look forward to turning their creative energy to the Park Wilshire. Moreover, with the explosion of new construction in both Downtown and Koreatown, they believe Westlake offers their tenants the ideal proximity to jobs, shopping and nightlife but with much greater character, charm and history that those other neighborhoods; therefore, the historic Westlake district offers amazing opportunity.

Sepulveda Blvd. in Los Angeles, CA. The sales price was reported at $68.2 million or $380.30/SF. The subject property was 81.5% leased at the time of sale. The property contains no deferred maintenance.

The in-place cap rate was reported at 4.3%; therefore, we were able to calculate the NOI. The market vacancy at 5%, total operating expenses at $17.15 after the re-assessed property taxes; therefore, we were able to calculate an approximate GSI.

Located immediately adjacent to the 405 Freeway near its intersection with the 10 Freeway, Sepulveda Center is a 12-story Class A office tower of high-quality office space and parking for 455 cars in a three-level garage and subterranean lot. The building's size and position next to the Westside's two major commute arteries, with an estimated 1.2 million cares passing it daily, give it unparalleled visibility. The property's excellent central Westside location and ease of freeway access make it an ideal choice for growing creative companies looking to attract and retain talent seeking an easier commute. 

The building sits close to both the Sepulveda and Palms stations of the new Metro Expo line, and is within a few miles of Silicon Beach, home to more than 2,000 companies including high profile employers such as Google, Yahoo! and Sony as well as a new generation of start-ups and one of the LA market's most vigorous leasing markets.

The motivation for the seller was the end of their hold period.

The motivation for the buyer was an opportunity to own and add value to a high quality building at the center of expanding Westside business community and close to Playa Vista, Culver City, the Wilshire Corridor, Westwood and Century City, but the occupancy costs that are significantly lower than these other markets. The property's convenient location, ease of access to major freeways and public transit, unobstructed outlooks, ample parking and efficient floor plates also add to its appeal as a compelling business location. Moreover, the acquisition represents yet another strategic addition to their Los Angeles portfolio which includes Bristol 61 in Culver City as well as major assets in downtown LA and Pasadena. As they have done with most of their other assets, they plan to make enhancements to the property that they believe will elevate the building's position within the market and make it attractive to a broad range of tenants including creative users such as entertainment, media/digital and advertising companies as well as the firms servicing these types of occupiers. This was their upleg in a 1031 exchange.

The Avalon at Royal Oaks sold for $27.55 million, or approximately $63,000 per unit, for the 436-unit apartment community.

In a statement on their web site, the buyer reported the acquisition cost at $30 million, or $68,807 per unit; sources indicated that there were reductions and credits, including for deferred maintenance, and that the $27.55 million price is more accurate.

The property, located on a 14.33-acre parcel, delivered in 1978. Occupancy, based on the rent roll, was reported to be +/-80% but was actually somewhat lower, about 75%. (The on-site property manager reported 80 units vacant, or about 18% of the total, shortly after the sale closed.) 

The seller had managed the property since acquiring it in 2012, and the relatively high vacancy was attributed to the lack of professional management. According to research at the time of the last sale, occupancy was basically unchanged between the two transactions, with 81% occupancy reported in March 2012.

There was notable deferred maintenance, with costs to cure pegged at +/-$2 million, including needed upgrades to electrical systems.

Trailing NOI was difficult to determine due to the management issues. Projected NOI at stabilization is $2.7 million, or about a 9.8% pro forma cap rate on the reported purchase price.

Rents, from the property manager, were reported at $956 per month the week of sale; they had been at $970 per month in August.

The purchase was financed with a $20 million bridge loan. It was noted that the property did not qualify for agency debt because of the vacancy issues.

The transaction was described as off-market. Reportedly, the buyer came close to acquiring Avalon at Royal Oaks at the end of 2015 but the deal fell through.

notes.value:
This transaction represents a merger sale of which included office, retail space, and non-rentable improvements such as parking garages. The properties are located in Texas, Arizona, Florida, Georgia, North Carolina, and Pennsylvania.  The sale consisted of 42 buildings approximately 13,324,717ft². However, the sellers website show 13,389,862ft². The difference of 65,145ft² may include parking garages and or storage facilities.   At the time of the merger the portfolio had an average occupancy of 90.9%, and leased 92.8%. The cap rate was 6.84%.

On October 6, 2016 the merger was completed. Each Parkway Properties share holder received 1.63 shares of Cousins Stock for a total consideration valued at approximately $1.89 billion. Also with the merger Cousins Properties assumed $1.1 billion in mortgage debt and $543.742 million in Credit facility debt which equates to an approximate purchase consideration of $3,533,742,000. 

Parkway Properties and Cousins Properties entered into a Merger Agreement on April 28, 2016, in which the operation of two companies will combine. The operations of the combined Houston portfolio will simultaneously spin-off into a separate public company (See comparable report 3722659 in reference to the Houston Co spin-off).  According the Cousins Properties SEC Filing, they incurred $2.4 million of merger costs in 2Q2016 related to the proposed merger with Parkway Properties Inc. With the completion of the spin-off Cousins and Parkway shareholders will own approximately 52% and 48%, respectively, of both Cousins and Houston Co.

Cousins Properties acquired 100% interest of the properties in the Parkway/Cousins Merger. However, Cousins only acquired a partial interest in the following properties due to previous Joint Venture deals:  Hayden Ferry Lakeside 30% interest (4 properties), Peachtree 33% interest (3 properties), and Two Liberty Place 19% interest. Also in addition, Parkway Properties sold an 80% of the Courvoisier Centre in February, 2016- (See comparable report 3514109 for further details).

As of the date of publication neither the deeds nor deed of trust(s) were located in public record. The portfolio NOI was approximately $241,830,000.

The information in this comparable report was obtained via: SEC Filings, Press releases, principles website(s), and public record. 

* The cap rate and NOI were based on the annualized figures of trailing 3 months (1Q2016).

This is a non-market transaction. On October 6, 2016 Cousins Properties Incorporated closed its previously announced merger with Parkway Properties Inc. On the following day, October 7, a spin-off company was created comprised of the Houston, Texas-based assets of the combined company. This new, publicly-traded REIT is called Parkway, Inc. The combined gross asset values of these properties as of December 31, 2015 was $2.2 billion.

The portfolio is comprised of five properties encompassing 8.7 million rentable square feet in the Galleria, Greenway and Westchase submarkets of Houston.

Under the terms of the spin-off, Cousins stockholders received one share of the Parkway, Inc. stock for every eight shares of Cousins common stock held as of the merger. Cousins common stockholders received cash in lieu of any fractional shares they would have been entitled to receive in the distribution.

In a presentation to their shareholders pre-merger, Cousins estimated the combined NOI of the Parkway, Inc. assets at $167 million, with no adjustments to NOI as a result of purchase accounting. Also reported was a $150 million initial cash balance and an additional $50 million undrawn credit facility. They show no debt maturing until 2018 and assume a $350 million term loan to be funded at closing.

The sale is comprised of Airport Center Building III, an office building totaling 306,234 SF located at 9841 Airport Blvd. in Los Angeles, CA. The sales price was reported at $12.5 million or $41/SF. The sale is a ground leased (Leasehold) interest; therefore, only the improvements sold. There is a 99-year ground lease in-place. The subject property was 62% leased at the time of sale; therefore, due to the high vacancy, a cap rate was not-applicable. The property needed major rehab work that included just about everything such as new roof, new elevators, new HVAC, interior and exterior work, etc. estimated at $8 million.

The property is located along Century Blvd. in the Los Angeles International Airport (LAX) submarket. The property benefits from its proximity to the airport and numerous affluent coastal neighborhoods as well as excellent access to the 105 and 405 freeways.

Century Blvd. has recently undergone a dramatic transformation as several competitive office buildings in the area have been converted into hotels, which has reduced office supply and improved the amenity base. In addition, an extension of the Metro Green Line is under construction, and the new station at the intersection of Century and Aviation Blvds., scheduled to open in 2019, is a short walk from the property. The completion of this station will be the first among many new public infrastructure projects in and around LAX including a new rental car facility an automated people mover connecting connecting the airport with the metro line and a second green line station at 96th and Aviation.

The reposition plan envisioned by TRG and Roxborough includes a complete rebranding, cosmetic upgrades to the exterior, a full renovation of the office lobby and entrance as well as improvements to the signage and landscaping. The repositioning is designed to transform the asset and take advantage of the lack of quality office space available in the submarket while offering rents at a discount to the neighboring submarkets.

The motivation for the seller was looking to monetize the asset.

The motivation for the buyer was the property is located in a unique coastal location experiencing dramatic changes, yet remains an affordable option for tenants priced out of Playa Vista, El Segundo and other Westside Silicon Beach submarkets. LAX is rapidly improving submarket that is well positioned to continue improvement. They are excited to be partnering with The Ruth Group, whose successful experiences in Southern California will be critical as they revitalize this asset. The property market the first acquisition for the partners, whose business plan calls for a significant renovation of the office building. Both are excited about the opportunity to reposition this landmark asset with a number of creative alternatives. This is a unique situation where they can begin to transform a submarket with the repositioning of a major asset that will thrive with the $14 billion expansion of LAX and the public transportation system.

TRG has proven success in the South Bay submarket with major repositions including 211 Ocean in Long Beach and The Knox in Torrance and plans to bring that direct expertise to the property.

A deed is unavailable at this time.

Villa Edgemont is located in Los Feliz, one of Los Angeles' most dynamic and desirable neighborhoods that strategically connects Hollywood to Silverlake. The property features a mix of studio, one bedroom and two bedroom units. Built in 1959, the property's unique layout features cascading levels that maximize stunning views of Griffith Park, Hollywood Hills and the Hollywood sign from throughout the property. The property also offers desirable community amenities including an abundance of courtyard community space, rooftop pool and sundeck with BBQ area, a fitness center and immediate access to nearby Barnsdall Art Park. 

Villa Edgemont is also considered a walker's paradise with a Walkscore of 93, according to Walkscore.com. From the property, residents can walk to numerous restaurants and nightlife venues along Hollywood, Vermont and Franklin Avenues including neighborhood hotspots such as II Capriccio, 1739 Public House, Starbucks, Umami Burger, Covell, The Dresden and Homestate. Additionally, Villa Edgemont offers access to public transit via the nearby Metro Red Line Vermont/Sunset station, connecting residents to Union Station and all other Metro lines.

The motivation for the seller was reorganization of capital.

The motivation for the buyer was to get a stronger foothold in Hollywood, and a value-add opportunity through a renovation program and lease-up. The vacancy was higher than normal due to those units being rent controlled, so they had to wait for the tenant to move-out, and kept vacant for the renovation program. Moreover, they are extremely comfortable investing in Hollywood and Los Feliz, and they will continue to build their portfolio of long-term holdings in these unique neighborhoods. They work from a disciplined investment model, one that create value through modernization, renovation and superior operation of well located apartment communities in market with high barriers to entry and existing or potential lifestyle appeal. The property meets all these criteria and offers a significant opportunity for rent growth in a market where they are very comfortable being long-term owners.

The portfolio includes about 14,000 rooms and is concentrated in California, Arizona and Texas.

Goldman Sachs' Whitehall Street Global Real Estate Fund started acquiring the portfolio in 2006 from the Tharaldson family.  In 2013, Goldman Sachs obtained $775 million in senior financing along with mezzanine financing totaling $560 million.  

Colony Northstar reported in their recent 2nd quarter earnings call "a basis of $92,000 per key and a 9% debt yield as of June 30, 2017 on depressed financial results."  They intend to sell the portfolio.

The property was initially a market rate/affordable community but the buyer has resyndicated the property as a LIHTC community with a 30-year tax credit compliance. The unit mix is comprised of 80 two-bedrooms, 92 three-bedrooms and 52 four-bedroom units. There was approximately 88% occupancy at the time of sale.

The buyer will be doing extensive renovations to the property that include unit interiors ($39K per door), upgraded amenities including a new pool, bus stop for residents and they will be knocking down the current clubhouse and rebuilding it entirely. Interiors renos will be done working by each building. 

The total improvement costs are nearly $9 million. The buyer used $16.5 million in tax-exempt financing to cover the acquisition, along with a $5.5 million construction loan that will be coverted to a permanent loan once renovations are completed. 

The seller was an affiliate of WillMax Capital Management. 

ARA Newmark's Austin and Houston offices brokered the deal.

The sales price was confirmed by the broker and the buyer's press release. The sale is comprised of the Santa Fe Lofts Apartments totaling 132 units located at 121 E. 6th St. in Los Angeles. The sales price was reported at $68,747,000 that equates to $520,811 per unit. The property also includes 13,500 SF of retail space across 10 floors. The subject property was not listed on the market for sale; therefore, the sale was an off-market transaction.

Commissioned by notable industrialist William G. Kerckhoff and designed by prominent LA architecture firm Morgan and Walls, the Santa Fe Lofts feature neoclassical details including authentic hexagonal plaster columns, mosaic tile, oversized windows and light wells as well as 1910s-era lobbies, staircases and corridors. Constructed in 1908, with an annex added in 1916, the building was purchased in 1933 by the Santa Fe Railroad which occupied seven floors for over 50 years. In 2005, the interior of the annex was renovated and converted to housing.

Located in the Gallery Row District of Downtown Los Angeles, the Santa Fe Lofts are situated in a walkable, Metro-accessible neighborhood that is brimming with art galleries, yoga studios, coffeehouses, restaurants, bars and the monthly Downtown Art Walk. The building itself includes nine commercial spaces occupied by prominent retail tenants including Las Perlas, the nation's first Mezcal bar, Pussy and Pooch, a modern pet boutique and groomer, and Redline Food and Bar, as well as two beauty salons. With their close proximity to the Financial District and Civic Center, the Santa Fe Lofts are ideally located for residents who want to work, live and recreate in Downtown Los Angeles. City officials are planning major upgrades to intersections and bike lanes in the area and recently approved the development of 1.2 million SF of new office, increased housing, retail and public open space in the Civic Center which borders the Historic Core of Downtown Los Angeles. 

The motivation for the buyer was a strong addition to their growing portfolio of properties with historical architectural details and community significance. The acquisition is a value-add opportunity through a renovation program. They look forward to providing the modern amenities and welcoming feel that renters value while restoring and showcasing the unique qualities that make the Santa Fe Lofts a standout property. They plan to invest over $6 million to rehabilitate and upgrade the property into a boutique residential community, constructing a state-of-the-art fitness center, refreshing the roof deck, upgrading elevator access and exterior renovations. They will integrate the building's ornate, classical design with modern amenities and hip communal spaces. 

Santa Fe Lofts is one of the largest multifamily adaptive reuse deals to sell since 2012, and is the fifth largest adaptive reuse multifamily project in all of Downtown Los Angeles. With the addition of Santa Fe Lofts, the buyer has acquired and invested in rehabilitating nine historic buildings across Los Angeles including the San Fernando Building, Wilshire Royale, Hollywood Tower and Park Wilshire.

Regent Garden Apartments, a 33-unit value add opportunity in the Palms neighborhood of the City of Los Angeles and just a short walk to Downtown Culver City. The property has a walkscore of 94, meaning that it is a walker's paradise and is primed to take advantage of the revitalization of Culver City which is directly adjacent to the property . 
The property is located within walking distance to both the Palms Metro Station and Culver City Metro Station along the Expo Line. In addition the property is walking distance to the highly anticipated 500,000 square foot Ivy Station which is a $300 million development that will include 200 residences, 200,000 square foot office building, 148 room boutique hotel, and over 50,000 square feet of retail. Ivy Station is the centerpiece of a $1 billion transit-oriented cluster covering about 20 acres surrounding the station and around the Expo Line. Ivy Station will also have a park-like public space that could hold as many as 800 people for a concert and will hold events such as dance classes, jazz performances and movie nights where shows will be projected on an inflatable theater screen. 
Other nearby developments include the Cumulus, a 1.9 million square foot development located at the intersection of Jefferson & La Cienega, which will include a seven-story podium building, a 30-story high rise building, about 1,200 residential units, and 100,000 square feet of retail. The Cumulus development will also include a 1-acre public park plaza. Just a short walk from Regent Gardens, the Culver Steps development is underway which is located between Trader Joe's and Culver Hotel and in front of the Culver Studios. The Culver Steps will have expansive public open space, 75,000 square feet of offices above 40,000 square feet of retail and restaurant space, plus a 35,000 square foot public plaza. 
Culver City is experiencing explosive growth with the influx of major entertainment and tech companies such as Amazon Studios, Apple and Beats by Dre. Culver City has a low unemployment rate of 3.8% with a future job growth projection of 38.95% over the course of the next ten years according to Bestplaces.net.
The cap rate is based on the sellers information on a trailing one year NOI.

On December 7, 2018 Brookfield Management acquired Forest City Realty Trust properties for a confirmed purchase price of $11.4 billion with a 4.75% portfolio cap rate, NOI $541,958,540.

The portfolio includes multiple property types. The assets are located in the following states: California, Colorado, Connecticut, Illinois, Massachusetts, Maryland, New Jersey, New York, Ohio, Pennsylvania, Rhode Island, Texas, and Washington D.C. Markets.  The sale consisted of 6.3 million square feet of high-quality office space, 2.2 million square feet of retail space, 18,500 multifamily units. The sale also included five large-scale development projects as follows:

·5M-San Francisco, CA- Mixed-use downtown project consisting of an office building 633,000ft² and an apartment building with approximately 295 units/doors. ·Pier 70-San Francisco. CA- Master Development of 28 acres to consist of approximately 3.2 million ft² mix-use property of office and retail space. 

·Hudson Exchange - Jersey City, NJ- the project is expected to include up to 5,400 apartment units in twelve towers and 350,000 square feet of amenity retail and dining space.

 ·Pacific Park Brooklyn - Brooklyn, NY- a 22-acre mixed-use project, expected to feature more than 6,400 units of housing, including 2,250 affordable units, and more than 8 acres of landscaped open space.  Included in the square feet of residential entitlements is 250,000 square feet of amenity retail

.·The Yards - Washington, D.C. - expected to include up to 3,000 residential units, 1.8 million square feet of office space and approximately 500,000 square feet of retail and dining space. 

-Waterfront Station - Washington, D.C.- expected to include 980 apartmentUnits/doors and approximately 50,000 square feet of retail stores and restaurants (according to the sellers Subsidiaries Supplemental Operating Information).

Forest City Realty Trust ownership of the individual properties included in the portfolio ranged from 30% to 100%.

Forest City Realty Trust Inc. founded in 1920 by Charles, Leonard, Max and Fannye Ratner. The company was a real estate investment trust that acquired, operated and managed commercial and residential real estate as well as land throughout the United States. 

Brookfield Asset Management founded in 1899, by William Mackenzie and Frederick Stark Pearson and headquartered in Brookfield Place, Toronto and it also has corporate offices in New York City, London, Rio de Janeiro and Sydney. The global company also trade as TSX, NYSE, Euronext and S&P/TSX.

29th Street Capital (29SC), a privately-held real estate operator, has acquired 14220 at Park Row Apartments, a 1998 vintage, 318-unit multifamily community located in West Houston. The sale price is an approximate from a source deemed reliable. The property was about 97% occupied at the time of sale.  The recorded docs were not available at the time of this publication.

29SC plans to re-brand the property and implement a smart technology upgrade program. 
“We are excited to add this asset to our Houston portfolio,” said Doug Burt, Vice President of Acquisitions in Houston. “The property will benefit from continued employment growth in the energy sector and lack of new supply coming to the submarket.
14220 at Park Row Apartments is located just off of I-10 along the Houston Energy Corridor. The corridor is now estimated to be the second-largest employment center in the Houston metropolitan area. It is home to over 300 companies, 107,000 employees and 27.1 million square feet of office space that is expected to reach 45.2 million square feet by 2030.
“The Energy Corridor took a hit a couple of years ago as the oil markets compressed,” Burt added. “With the market recovering and the area gaining those jobs back, we feel the submarket is poised for continued economic expansion.” 
This is the tenth acquisition in the Houston area in the past five years. Formed in 2009, 29th Street Capital is a privately-held real estate investment and advisory firm that employs a value-added investment strategy in acquiring properties that typically fall below the radar of its institutional peers. Over the past 12 months 29th Street Capital has also acquired 18 conventional multifamily assets and continues to actively pursue additional opportunities throughout the U.S. 
29SC’s conventional multifamily portfolio currently consists of more than 8,700 units having acquired over 15,800 units across its 15 offices in the U.S. Investments typically require approximately $10 million to $100 million of total capital and involve the acquisition or recapitalization of individual real estate assets, portfolios or platforms.

The sales price was confirmed by the listing broker's press release and one of the sellers. The sale is comprised of the Airport Center Building III totaling 306,243 SF located at 5901 W. Century Blvd. in Los Angeles, CA. The sales price was reported at $45 million or $147/SF. The subject property was 92% leased at the time of sale. The in-place cap rate was reported at 6.7% at the time of sale; however, the buyer is obligated for seismic upgrades that need to be taken on that shows the cap rate closer to 6.15%.

The 15-story office tower is located along Century Blvd. in the LAX submarket. Along with recent building systems upgrades, the property has been heavily rebranded and features a newly renovated lobby and common areas, an executive clubhouse, dog park and a bicycle-sharing program.

The property benefits from its proximity to LAX and to numerous affluent coastal neighborhoods as well as excellent access to the 105 and 405 freeways. Century Blvd. has recently undergone a dramatic transformation as several competitive office buildings in the area have been converted into hotels which also reduced the office supply and improved the amenity base. In addition, an extension of the Metro Green Line at the intersection of Century and Aviation is a short walk from the property. The completion of this station was the first amongst many new public infrastructure projects in and around LAX, including a new rental care facility, and automated people mover connecting the airport with the metro line, and a green line station at 96th and Aviation. 

With the property situated between two of the most exciting markets in Los Angeles, immediately south of the Silicon Beach and just north of El Segundo, the property offers exceptional regional access and proximity to executive housing in the South Bay. Coupled with the nearby $14B capital improvement plan currently underway at LAX and the excitement surrounding the new LA Stadium and Entertainment District, and the LAX submarket will continue to attract quality tenants searching for an economic alternative to the more expensive surrounding areas.

The seller acquired the asset in early 2017 and invested in excess of $8 million to renovate and reposition the property. The seller completed more than 220,000 SF of new leases, expansions and renewals during that short timeframe at rents up to and exceeding $3 FSG, which are historic highs and demonstrates amazing leasing velocity for this submarket. 

The motivation for the buyer was attracted to the tremendous mark to mark upside with the well below market average existing rents in conjunction with the great basis. 

A deed is unavailable at this time.

American Hotel Income Properties Trust REIT LP acquired a portfolio of twelve premium-branded hotels located in various states for $191 million, or about $158,769 per key, from Starwood Capital Group on December 3, 2019.

The properties were originally developed by TMI Hospitality, which was acquired in its entirety by Starwood Capital Group in 2014. (Starwood subsequently spun off and sold TMI Hospitality's operations to an affiliate of Aimbridge Hospitality, in June 2017. However, the real estate assets were still owned by Starwood Capital Group).

The portfolio has a total of 1203 keys.

The properties included in the sale were:

*500 Trade Centre Way in Portage, MI (Homewood Suites Kalamazoo Portage) (97 keys)
*185 Radio Drive in Woodbury, MN (Courtyard by Marriott St. Paul Woodbury) (120 keys)
*205 Radio Drive in Woodbury, MN (Residence Inn St.Paul Woodbury) (116 keys)
*3319 N 14th Street in Bismarck, ND (Courtyard by Marriott Bismarck North) (89 keys)
*1004 Sutherland Drive in Pittsburgh, PA (Fairfield Inn & Suites Pittsburgh Airport/Robinson Township) (103 keys)
*1006 Sutherland Drive in Pittsburgh, PA (TownePlace Suites Pittsburgh Airport/Robinson Township) (93 keys)
*5879 S Padre Island Drive in Corpus Christi, TX (Hampton Inn & Suites Corpus Christi) (101 keys)
*7815 Willow Chase Boulevard in Houston, TX (Home2Suites by Hilton Houston Willowbrook) (108 keys)
*1401 Catalina Drive in Midland, TX (Home2Suites by Hilton Midland) (93 keys)
*1505 Catalina Drive in Midland, TX (Staybridge Suites Midland) (98 keys)
*2545 Southwest Boulevard in San Angelo, TX (Residence Inn by Marriott San Angelo) (92 keys)
*2569 Southwest Boulevard in San Angelo, TX (Home2Suites by Hilton San Angelo) (93 keys)

The properties were sold in an off market transaction.

The seller and buyer represented themselves.

There were no conditions which affected the sale price.

The buyer took out a $105 million interest-only loan with a 5-year term to partially finance the acquisition. The buyer has entered into a swap rate agreement to secure the interest rate to a maximum of 3.52% for a period of 4 years.

The buyer acquired the portfolio less than a week after selling 45 economy lodging hotels to Vukota Capital Management for $215.5 million on November 28, 2019 (see CoStar COMP ID# 4964817). With the completion of both sales, the buyer nows intend to focus on growing their higher quality portfolio of 79 premium-branded select-service hotels. The acquisition also gives the buyer further gegraphic diversification of their properties in the United States and expands their portfolio of suites-focused and extended-stay hotels which have higher profit margins.

Press releases issued by the buyer confirmed the sale date, sale price, number of keys, the buyer's motivation, and some of the terms of the financing.

A source deemed reliable confirmed the sale date, sale price, number of keys, and the parties involved. The source was not at liberty to provide the cap rate.
