The sales price was confirmed by one of the brokers and the seller. The sale is comprised of The Pearl on Wilshire Apartments totaling 346 units located at 687 S. Hobart Blvd. in Los Angeles, CA. The sales price was reported at $170.87 million that equates to $493,844 per unit, which represents the full value of the property; however, the buyer acquired a 60% interest from their joint venture partner given they owned 40% at the time of sale. The subject property was approximately 98% leased at the time of sale. The first year pro forma cap rate was reported at approximately 4.2%. The property contains no sales conditions that would have affected the sales price, and contains no deferred maintenance.

The Pearl on Wilshire is a luxury mixed-used development in Los Angeles's Koreatown. Cityview developed the apartment community on land originally entitled by Hankey Investment Company and sold its interest to a group led by Hankey Investment Company. The Pearl on Wilshire achieved lease-up in 10 months at above pro forma rents after opening to tenants in the summer of 2018. Cityview partnered with CBG Building Company, VTBS Architects and Nadia Geller Designs on the original construction of the property, which was completed in June 2018.

The mixed-use development features 17 unique floor plans with a blend of studio, one- and two-bedroom units above 8,300 SF of retail space. All units feature keyless door locks, a full-sized washer and dryer, stainless steel appliances, a five-burner gas range, smart thermostat, quartz countertops and a terrace, while select units feature high ceilings, oversized balconies and panoramic city views of Koreatown. An Orangetheory Fitness , Alchemist Coffee Project and The Carving Board artisan sandwich shop cater to residents and the community in the ground-floor retail portion of the building.

Community amenities include a large pool deck with cabanas and lounge seating, rooftop terrace with a fireplace and sweeping city views, Korean BBQ grills, game and club room, state-of-the-art fitness center with a yoga room and Fitness On-Demand, dog agility center and grooming spa and three open-air lounges with firepits and a bocce ball court.

The Think Space conference room and 24-hour business center, with computers and printers, add extra conveniences for professionals working remotely. The Pearl's lobby features an Uber/Lyft waiting area, complimentary Wi-Fi, charging stations, 24-hour concierge, secure fob entry access and a grab-and-go coffee bar. For the conveniences of its residents, the community also coordinates lifestyle services such as dog walking, dry cleaning and housekeeping services.

IN 2019 the community was awarded the Kingsley Excellence Award, a recognition that distinguishes communities that outperform the Kingsley Index Industry benchmark for overall resident satisfaction. The Pearl is also pending Fitwel certification for its focus on residents' health and wellbeing, as evidenced by its walk score of 97, convenient access to public transportation and large indoor bicycle storage facility.

The motivation for the seller was a merchant builder that developed the property, stabilized it and then sold the asset as part of their business plan. The community exceeded their lease-up expectations and was sold at a record breaking price psf. They are closing the fund.

The motivation for the buyer was they liked the asset and location.

A deed is unavailable at this time.

The sales price was confirmed by the broker's press release and the seller. The sale is comprised of the Park Wilshire Apartments totaling 170 units located at 2424 Wilshire Blvd. in Los Angeles, CA. The sales price was reported at $38.2 million that equates to $224,706 per unit. The subject property was 95% leased at the time of sale. The in-place cap rate was reported at 4.4%. The buyer assumed an existing loan on the property from Wells Fargo Bank.

Park Wilshire is one of just a handful of restored Jazz Age-era buildings left in Los Angeles. Over the past few years, prior ownership made significant capital expenditures to renovate the common areas, amenities and 82 units to a high-level, luxury specification. 

Westlake is one of the most densely populated urban areas in the country and is arguably Los Angeles' strongest rental market with approximately 96% of residents living in renter-occupied housing. Throughout most of the decade, occupancy has been above 95% and is projected to remain at that level into the foreseeable future. The property is located adjacent to MacArthur Park and about a mile from Downtown and Mid-Wilshire/Koreatown, home to 72 million SF of combined office space. The Westlake/MacArthur Park Metro station is nearby and the 110 and 101 freeways are within 1.5 miles.

Centered between two of Los Angeles' most dynamic neighborhoods, the property provides residents with convenient access to some of Los Angeles' largest employers. Built in 1924. the building blends original Italian Renaissance Revival details with high-end contemporary amenities. The property has marble floors, crown moldings, floor-to-ceiling arched windows, and ornamented ceilings. The unit mix features five floor plans and a mix of studio, one- and two-bedroom apartments. A 14,002 SF parking lot behind the building is zoned for development of up to 60 apartments.

The motivation for the seller was the end of their hold period.

The motivation for the buyer was the property will be a good addition to their multifamily holdings in Los Angeles. They were able to close this transaction in seven days, and it is the 7th transaction they have completed in the last five months with over $250 million in acquisitions for this period.

At time of sale the property was 81% occupied. The investment property sold with a cap rate at time of sale, "north of 11.00%", producing a minimum NOI of $404,250. The property is located within the three-building office park, Intercontinental Park. The three-story Class B office property was built in 1982, and is situated on a 3.63 acre parcel. The property is also located within a Federal Opportunity Zone. This was the buyer's upleg on a 1031 Exchange. 

 Listing broker reports:

Intercontinental Park III is a ±88,551 RBA Class A, 3-story, office building located at 16701 Greenspoint Park Drive in Houston, TX. This asset gives investors the opportunity to purchase a cash flowing office building with upside opportunities within the Greenspoint/N Belt West Submarket. Originally built in 1982 and extensively renovated since, this multi-tenant office building contains ±88,551 RBA within a well maintained 3 building office park in the heart of North Houston. The Building contains 17 office units ranging in size from ±824 to ±20,623 SF. The Property has had numerous recently completed capital improvements including perimeter fencing (±$190k), lighting upgrade for surface parking (±41k), monument signage (±25), energy management HVAC (±55k), lobby directory board (±12k) and upgraded 3rd floor restrooms (±80k). The Property is ±81% occupied by a mix of professional office users with staggered lease expirations, escalations, and options. Intercontinental Park III offers a unique opportunity for owner occupants to absorb some vacancy and also offers future value enhancement via mark-to-market rates upon rollover (estimated at $16.50/SF Full Service Gross in the submarket according to CoStar data). The Property is well-positioned to take advantage of sustained tenant demand and rent growth into the foreseeable future. Additionally, the Property benefits from its location within a Federal Opportunity Zone and offers investors incentives for putting their capital to work including a temporary tax deferral for capital gains reinvested in an Opportunity Fund; A step-up in basis for capital gains reinvested in an Opportunity Fund; and a permanent exclusion from taxable income of capital gains from the sale or exchange of an investment in a qualified opportunity zone fund, if the investment is held for at least 10 years. Intercontinental Park III is in a robust trade area near a mix of hospitality, retail, office and industrial and offers excellent accessibility with convenient access to major thoroughfares including Sam Houston Tollway, I-45, Highway 59 and Grand Parkway. Additionally, Intercontinental Park III benefits from its location near economic drivers including Greenspoint Mall (±0.7 mi), Bush Intercontinental Airport (±12-min), W. W. Thorne Stadium (±3 mi), and Lone Star College North Harris (±15-min) to name a few. The Property is poised to benefits from its location in a high traffic area with ±135,483 VPD at the intersection of Beltway 8 and Imperial Valley Drive, just ±0.15-mi East of the Property (2020). The North Houston area offers a variety of full and limited service hotels that meet the needs of both visitors and business travelers. With a close proximity to Bush IAH and the ability to get almost anywhere in Houston in less than 30 minutes, the area is an ideal location for business meetings, conventions or hotel stays. Intercontinental Park III is located across the street from a Hilton and Marriott which offer the opportunity for discounted and free shuttles to IAH.

On August 3, 2021, the merger between Kimco Realty and Weingarten Realty was approved. The transaction included a reported $3.9 billion equity value and $5.9 billion transaction value.  In the agreement Weingarten merged with and into Kimco, with Kimco continuing as the surviving public company.

The buyer Kimco Realty Corp. (NYSE: KIM), is one of North America’s largest publicly traded owners and operators of open-air, grocery-anchored shopping centers and mixed-use assets.

The seller Weingarten Realty Investors (NYSE: WRI), was a grocery-anchored Sun Belt shopping center owner, manager and developer. 

Pursuant to the terms of the definitive merger agreement entered by and between Kimco and Weingarten on April 15, 2021, Weingarten shareholders are entitled to receive 1.408 newly issued shares of Kimco common stock plus $2.20 in cash, after adjustment for the Weingarten special dividend of $0.69 per Weingarten common share paid on August 2, for each Weingarten common share that they owned immediately prior to the effective time of the merger. Upon completion of the merger, the common stock of the combined company will trade under the symbol “KIM” on the NYSE, and Weingarten’s common shares will be suspended from trading on the NYSE effective as of the opening of trading on August 4, 2021, per SEC Filing.

On June 30, 2021, Weingarten owned or operated under long-term leases, either directly or through its interest in real estate joint ventures or partnerships, a total of 155 properties which are in 15 states spanning the country from coast to coast. These properties represent approximately 29.7 million square feet of which our interests in these properties aggregated approximately 20.3 million square feet of leasable area. Weingarten assets had 92.9% Operating Portfolio Occupancy, 82% % of ABR from Grocery Anchored Centers, $718/SF AVG Grocery Sales/SF, $20.43 ABR/SF.

The combined company is expected to benefit from increased scale and density in key Sun Belt markets, enhanced asset quality, tenant diversity, a larger redevelopment pipeline and a deleveraged balance sheet. As a result, the combined company should be uniquely positioned to drive further sustained growth in net operating income (NOI) and asset value creation through continued strategic leasing and asset management. 


The increased scale in targeted growth markets, coupled with a broader pipeline of redevelopment opportunities, positions the company to create significant value for its shareholders. The combined company is expected to have a pro forma equity market capitalization of approximately $12.0 billion and a pro forma total enterprise value of approximately $20.5 billion.

“We are pleased to announce the successful completion of our merger with Weingarten” stated Conor Flynn, Chief Executive Officer of Kimco. “This strategic combination, designed to drive long-term growth and value creation, results in an expanded and more diversified portfolio with embedded growth opportunities while further strengthening our financial profile. We look forward to the rapid integration of our platforms across our key Sun Belt markets, the realization of signification economies of scale, and the extraordinary potential of untapped redevelopment opportunities.”

The winning bid at $6,646,250 includes a auction fee of (%).  At time of sale property was open dba Homewood Suites by Hilton Houston West-Energy Corridor. The buyer plans to spend up to $1.1M or $15,000 per key on a PIP. Current room rates at $106/King Bed studio and $121 for two queens. 

Broker reports:
A new investor can expect a new 15-year franchise license agreement with Hilton upon completion of the brand-mandated change-of-ownership PIP, estimated at $1,100,000 or $15,000 per key (PIP report has been ordered and will be posted to the due diligence documents upon receipt). In 2020, current ownership spent about $500,000 to paint all guestrooms, replace carpet and flooring in the common areas, lobby furniture, dining area, suite shop, and fitness center to brand standards. This offering presents an excellent opportunity for a private investor to enter the Hilton brand family with a highly sought-after extended-stay product at a price well below replacement cost. At the peak of the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020, extended-stay hotels performed significantly better than other asset types. This hotel provides a new investor with the security of owning a recession-resistant product. The all-suite design promotes guest independence, which yields lower housekeeping costs and potentially higher profits. The hotel has experienced a strong rebound in room revenues over the last two months, with 2021 monthly room revenues exceeding 2019 numbers by an average of over 20% per month. This trend is expected to continue throughout the remainder of the year, and the asset is on pace to return to pre-COIVD levels by the end of 2021. Over the last three years, the hotel has registered an average GOP of less than 30%. Based on a selection of similar vintage Homewood Suites by Hilton operating statements, the hotel should achieve a stabilized GOP margin between 48% and 52%. Great upside exists for a more hands-on operator to restructure the hotel

Sentinel Real Estate Corporation (“Sentinel”)  has acquired Three Thousand Sage, a 324-unit mid-rise apartment community in Houston for undisclosed price. The transaction presented an opportunity for Sentinel to acquire a high-quality asset where it can leverage its extensive operational expertise to implement a capital improvement program intended to enhance income and the value of the investment.

“In Three Thousand Sage, we have recognized an opportunity to acquire a high-quality asset in a desirable market that has seen significant increases in demand driven by consistently strong job and population growth,” said Michael Streicker, President of Sentinel. “Multifamily vacancy rates are currently at their lowest point since 2015, and the region saw 20,000 net move-ins in the first half of 2021 – the strongest two quarters on record. The property is well positioned to capitalize on that demand, ideally situated in the heart of several high-profile employment hubs in Houston. This acquisition exemplifies our proven investment strategy, and we look forward to making improvements that create an even better place for our residents to live.”

Built in 2004, Three Thousand Sage is a four-story, 324-unit apartment complex comprising one- and two-bedroom units averaging 1,006 square feet. Each residence features high-quality finishes such as nine- and 10-foot ceilings, granite countertops, large garden tubs, hardwood-style floors, walk-in closets, full-sized washer-dryers and intrusion alarms. Select units include stainless steel appliances, a private patio or balcony, a private office with built-in computer desk, glass front cabinets, double vanities in the bathrooms and travertine flooring. Community amenities include two resort-style pools, a cabana with gas grills, a well-appointed fitness center, two resident lounges, and an electronic parcel locker system.

The sale is comprised of the Wilshire Royale Apartments totaling 193 units with 8,933 SF of ground floor retail located at 2619 Wilshire Blvd. in the Westlake District of  Los Angeles, CA. The sales price was reported $45.5 million that equates to $235,751 per unit.

Originally constructed as the upscale Arcady apartment-hotel, the property exemplifies the opulence of Neoclassical, Beaux Arts architecture and has been extensively renovated to provide the ultimate living experience in a submarket with compelling demand drivers. 

Built in 1927, the property has become an iconic landmark in the Westlake neighborhood and is one of only a handful of restored neoclassical buildings left in Los Angeles. The property contains a 14,757 SF rear parking lot that qualifies for a Transit Oriented Communities Tier 3 density bonus, allowing for an up to 63-unit multifamily development.

Located one mile from Downtown Los Angeles and Mid-Wilshire/Koreatown, which have 78 million SF of combined office space. The property residents can easily reach some of Los Angeles's largest employers. The property is within 1.5 miles of both Interstate 110 and U.S. Highway 101, which provides access to employment hubs throughout Southern California. The Wilshire/Vermont and Westlake/MacArthur metro stations are a short walk away and vibrant retail, restaurant and nightlife in Silver Lake, Koreatown and Downtown Los Angeles are close by.

The property's floorplans include efficiencies, studios, one-bedroom, two-bedroom and three-bedroom layouts. The renovated apartment units have hardwood vinyl plank flooring, stainless steel appliances, two-tone point, luxurious hardware, crown moldings, contemporary lighting fixtures, ceiling fans and walk-in closets. The fully renovated community amenities include a fitness center, a designer-decorated resident lounge, a conference rooms, business center, swimming pool and space, 24-hour valet parking and sweeping downtown views.

The motivation for the seller was they completed a value-add revitalization project as part of their improvement vision. Consistent with other historic projects they have completed in the past, their strategy of making exciting, historically accurate upgrades has brought tremendous value to the property and the surrounding submarket. The expansive grand lobby, which features dramatic marble stairways and ornate columns and archways, was infused with furnishings and decor from the former Figueroa Hotel. Additionally, they restored the famous rooftop neon sign, completed premium lighting upgrades to the exterior facade, refreshed the outdoor pool area and courtyard, and transformed the building corridors and apartment interiors by merging vintage details with contemporary finishes.

The motivation for the buyer was a value-add opportunity to generate additional revenue by continuing the high-end unit interior renovation program and furthering enhance the income stream through the redevelopment of the ground floor retail space and 4,500 SF of basement.

The recorded seller ownership interest as follows:

Wilshire Royale Pacific LLC     40%
One Eleven Tampa LLC     60%

The sales price was reported at $28.7 million that equates to $486,441 per unit. The subject property was 95% leased at the time of sale. The in-place cap rate was reported at 3.9%. The property contains no deferred maintenance.

During the lockdowns due to the pandemic, Eagle Rock and Highland Park neighborhoods became especially preferred destinations for Downtown Los Angeles residents who wanted more space to maneuver after common areas and urban dining entertainment venues closed down. The neighborhoods also benefited from transplants from New York and San Francisco who felt like the area was a good balance between true urban core and suburban living. 

The Tenant Protection Act of 2019, which placed 80s and 90s multifamily product under state rent control, and the difficulties many developers are facing in acquiring land are motivation investors to redirect significant capital towards newly constructed assets. With rents currently below pre-Covid levels and cap rates hovering 300 basis points over the 10-year Treasury, newly constructed multifamily assets give investors the opportunity to keep pace with the market and generate attractive returns.

Constructed on almost an entire block along Eagle Rock Boulevard, the property is accessible from State Route 2, and Interstates 5, 110 and 134, which connect Eagle Rock with the surrounding employment hubs. The nearby Glendale Metrolink and Highland Park Gold Line stations provide residents with light rail access to myriad suburban and urban districts throughout Southern California.

The motivation for the seller was their downleg in a 1031 exchange.

The 544 unit Del Mar at 10919 Gulf Fwy in Houston, TX sold at an undisclosed price. The property was 84.49% occupied at the time of sale. 

The 419,316-square-foot community was sold by First Choice Management through a 1031 exchange. Three Pillars Capital Groupa acquired the multifamily asset.

"Houston is experiencing tremendous growth and demand for rental housing continues to soar as residents flee high costs of living in major gateway cities following the pandemic,” said Gautam Goyal, Founder and Managing Principal of Three Pillars Capital Group. “We are very proud of the acquisition of Del Mar Apartments. It's a large transaction and is further testament to our firm’s ability to create value for our renters and strong risk-adjusted returns for our investment partners.”

Goyal adds,“We acquired this community through a 1031 exchange, and have structured many deals in a similar fashion. A 1031 exchange allows investors to snowball their initial investment into something potentially larger, and it's a great vehicle for us because it brings in equity that we no longer have to raise. As demand for more moderately priced Class-B and Class-C housing across Houston increases due to rising rents spurred by inflation,  Del Mar Apartments will help meet the needs of residents in the current climate.”

Originally built in 1972, Three Pillars will oversee a strategic value-add repositioning of the community that will include the addition of granite countertops in kitchens and bathrooms, designer kitchen backsplashes and modern fixtures, as well as pull-down gooseneck faucets in kitchens. Additional upgrades will consist of vinyl wood-look flooring, crown molding, chair rail molding, new decorative interior doors and an updated interior paint scheme. Bathroom renovations will feature tiled bathtub surrounds, vessel sinks with modern single-handle faucets and framed mirrors. Additionally, showerheads, faucets and commodes will be replaced with updated water conserving variants. 

According to CoStar, investors have poured capital into Houston multifamily at a record pace over the past several quarters, eager to tap into the market's robust fundamentals and demographic trends. Many of the major apartment properties that have traded of late have involved well-located, value-add opportunities (properties rated 3 Star or less) and some larger Core Plus portfolios.

Per CoStar analytics, vacancies in the Houston market remain near seven-year lows, though annual net absorption has moderated from its historically strong level in 2021. Rent gains, too, have started to abate, but year-over-year rent growth of 5.3% is still well above historic norms. Above-average rent growth is prevalent in both urban and suburban settings.

While the metro's apartment sector remains healthy, there are 24,000 units under construction, and apartment owners will need to brace for a wave of deliveries over the next few quarters. This could result in more modest rent gains in the near term.

Heading into the second half of the year, it seems 2022 will be another record year for multifamily investment volume. CoStar estimates that multifamily investment volume totaled $18 billion during 2021, more than three times the average yearly volume ($5 billion) recorded between 2010 and 2019. CoStar estimates that multifamily investment volume totaled nearly $9 billion during the first half of 2022. That marks the highest total ever for the first half of a year to date.

National investors continue to drive investment volume in Houston, with out-of-state firms (including Blackstone, Berkshire, and TruAmerica Multifamily) accounting for more than 80% of buyer volume over the past four quarters. The Federal Reserve's recent interest rate hikes to curb 40-year high inflation is placing upward pressure on borrowing costs. Still, overall pricing remains elevated by historical standards and average market pricing is about 12% higher year over year.

- The Santa Rosalia Apartments, a two-story, 326-unit community located at 4220 Santa Rosalia Drive in Los Angeles's Baldwin Village; and

- The Santo Tomas Apartments, a two-story, 343-unit community located at 4318 Santo Tomas Drive in Los Angeles's Crenshaw neighborhood.

The seller was Calabasas, CA-based Upside Investments, Inc.  They originally purchased the properties in September 2013 for $60 million.

Upside aimed to sell using a unique structure that allows the new owners to provide the residents with a long-term affordable housing solution, according to a press release from their brokerage team on this transaction.

The buyer was Irvine, CA-based Avanath Capital Management, a firm specializing in affordable housing ownership and equity funding.

They are partnering with the Housing Authority of the City of Los Angeles (HACLA) and Kaiser Permanente in the acquisition.  As per HACLA's Housing Conduit Bond Policy, this partnership grants Avanath eligibility to turn 70% of the units into affordable housing and qualify for the California Tax Credit Allocation Committee’s LIHTC.

They plan to serve residents earning between 60% and 80% of area median income, allowing the firm to provide budget-friendly homes in one of the country’s least affordable rental markets, according to a press release from the buyer.

The information available on this sale comparable report was compiled via public record documents from the county records office and further confirmed by multiple sources deemed reliable.

**Please note that while press from the buyer states a price of $230 million, it was contradicted by representatives of the selling party, the purchasing party, and documentation from the county clerk office, all of which stated $220 million.

On August 4th, 2022, the 216-unit multifamily community Villa La Jolla in Houston, Texas sold for an undisclosed price. Located at 10101 Forum Park Drive, this class C community, delivered in 1979, sits on 6.91 acres and features a unit mix of one and tow- bedroom units ranging from 550 to 1,100 square feet. Rents range from $739 to $1,056 per unit. 

The buyer, Dallas-based WindMass Capital is a privately owned commercial real estate investment and development company. 

Per CoStar analytics, Vacancies remain near seven-year lows, though annual net absorption has moderated from its historically strong level in 2021. Rent gains, too, have started to abate, but year-over-year rent growth of 3.7% is still well above historic norms. Above-average rent growth is prevalent in both urban and suburban settings.

While the metro's apartment sector remains healthy, there are 23,000 units under construction, and apartment owners will need to brace for a wave of deliveries over the next few quarters. This could result in more modest rent gains in the near term.
Houston has frequently ranked among the top job and population growth metros in the country and, as such, lured apartment developers. From 2020-21, the metro ranked third in the country in nominal population growth, trailing only DFW and Phoenix, and up by around 70,000 new residents. Since 2010, the market has added more than 140,000 new multifamily units, growing its inventory by 30% and ranking among the top three markets in the country in terms of new supply during this time. The metro's strong population growth persists, as Houston continues to draw more residents from around the world, thanks to its cultural amenities, world-class restaurants, low cost of living, and ethnically diverse communities.

Sales volume in Houston's multifamily sector has accelerated at a record pace over the past several quarters, as investors are eager to tap into the market's robust fundamentals and demographic trends. Many of the major apartment properties that have traded of late have involved well-located, value-add opportunities (properties rated 3 Star or less) and some larger Core Plus portfolios. 

Heading into the end of the year, it seems 2022 will be another record year for multifamily investment volume. CoStar estimates that multifamily investment volume totaled $18 billion during 2021, more than three times the average yearly volume ($5 billion) recorded between 2010 and 2019. CoStar estimates that multifamily investment volume totaled nearly $9 billion during the first half of 2022. That marks the highest total ever for the first half of a year to date.

National investors continue to drive investment volume in Houston, with out-of-state firms (including Blackstone, Berkshire, and TruAmerica Multifamily) accounting for more than 80% of buyer volume over the past four quarters. The Federal Reserve's recent interest rate hikes to curb 40-year high inflation is placing upward pressure on borrowing costs. Still, overall pricing remains elevated by historical standards and average market pricing is about 12% higher year over year.

Parkway, Nuveen, and CPP Investments sold this approximate 5,751,918-square-foot, excluding parking garages,  mixed-use business campus on approximately 55 acres to Interra Properties LLC for an undisclosed price The portfolio includes multiple office towers, retail space, a health club, and dining amenities.

The property was under court-appointed receivership at the time of sale due to loan default in 2022.

 As part of the transaction, the buyer assumed the outstanding $416,200,000 CMBS loan, which had been reduced from the original $465,000,000 balance. 

The campus was approximately 70% occupied, with Occidental Petroleum as the largest tenant holding approximately 972,000 square feet under lease through 2031.

The buyer was drawn to the opportunity to acquire one of Houston's largest Inner Loop mixed-use campuses at a basis that allows for value-add repositioning and re-leasing strategies.

Please note that CoStar's total square footage for rentable buildings does not align with that of the parties involved in the transaction by approximately 1M square feet. These properties will be updated once information  is received. 

The information in the comparable has been verified by public record and press release.

Raintree Partners sold four student housing apartment buildings totaling 153 units to private investors for $62.5 million, or $409,150 per unit. According to CoStar data, the portfolio comprises 177 beds.

The four properties transacted separately with individual pricing. 415 Gayley Avenue sold for $18,125,000; 411 Kelton Avenue sold for $22,850,000; 555 Levering Avenue sold for $12.25 million; and 555 Kelton Avenue sold for $9,375,000.

The seller completed significant improvements to the properties, and they were marketed and sold as turnkey assets. The buyers were attracted to the acquisition due to supply constraints in the area and UCLA’s planned enrollment growth. The reported cap rate was 3.35%.

The acquisition was financed with a $65 million loan. Notably, the financing also supported an existing property within the buyer’s portfolio.

Wilshire Skyline, Inc. and CGI+ Real Estate Investments sold an 86-unit apartment complex to Faulkner Capital Partners for $33,884,000, or $394,000 per unit.

The sellers acquired the site in 2019 when it was a parking lot. Initial plans called for a 53-unit development, but the project was ultimately entitled for 86 units. Construction was completed in early 2024, and the property was beyond its lease-up phase at the time of sale. The reported cap rate was 5.5%.

IMT Residential sold the 392-unit Aston Post Oak multifamily community to a joint venture between Japanese real estate funds Kenedix and Hulic Co., Ltd., in partnership with Rockport Equity Partners, for an undisclosed price. 

The Class A asset totals approximately 415,160 square feet and was constructed in 2008 on a 4.465-acre site. At the time of sale, the property was 98% occupied and was marketed as a luxury residential community offering modern amenities in a prime Houston location. 

The buyer group was attracted to the asset’s position within Houston’s inner-ring submarket, where new multifamily supply is limited and demand is strong, and plans to complete capital upgrades focused on exterior improvements. 

Financing for the acquisition included a $54,075,000 senior loan provided by Regions Bank.

On April 20th, 2026, a private entity sold this 12-unit multifamily building to private investors for $7,600,000, or $633,333 per unit. The 16,860-square-foot asset was on the market for 314 days, with an initial asking price of $8,250,000. Built in 2015, the luxury asset features twelve two-bedroom, two-bathroom condo-style units ranging from 1,185 to 1,340 square feet. Residences offer floor-to-ceiling windows, 10-foot ceilings, designer kitchens with quartz countertops, stainless-steel appliances, in-unit washer/dryers, walk-in closets, and private balconies with fireplaces. Building amenities include controlled access, assigned garage parking with EV charging capabilities, and an elevated rooftop lounge with panoramic city views. The in-place net operating income was reported to be $433,353, yielding an actual cap rate of 5.7%. The information in the comparable has been verified by the listing broker.
This is a change in title vesting and should not be considered in market comparables.

Kilroy Realty Corporation sold two apartment towers totaling 393 units to Advanced Real Estate for $202 million, or $513,995 per unit.

Kilroy sold the 200-unit Sky Hollywood for $99 million, or $495,000 per unit, and the 193-unit Jardine Hollywood for $103 million, or $533,679 per unit. Both towers include penthouse units that reportedly lease for $12,000 to $20,000 per month.

The buyers cited the limited supply of apartment towers in Hollywood, as well as anticipated demand associated with upcoming global events such as the World Cup and Olympics, as key motivations for the acquisition.

The acquisition was financed with two interest-only loans totaling $141,400,000, with a reported interest rate of 5.17%.

Madison Marquette and National Real Estate Advisors sold a 254-unit, 40-story luxury apartment tower to Vero Sade for $168,000,000, equating to $661,417 per unit. The asset, completed in 2015 utilizing steel construction, contains 392,266 square feet and is situated on a 2.6-acre site.

The property features a mix of one-, two-, and three-bedroom floor plans in addition to penthouse residences. Rents range from $2,250 per month for entry-level units to $13,000 per month for penthouse units. Amenities include an outdoor tenant lounge, swimming pool, fitness center, conference center, and dog park. The property was originally developed by PM Realty Group, which is now known as Madison Marquette.

Following the acquisition, Vero Sade outlined an $11,000,000 capital improvement program covering 20,836 square feet. Planned upgrades include a first-floor remodel, replacement of exterior window walls and canopy, installation of new garage screens on floors two through eight, construction of new roof screen walls, and replacement of exterior walls on the eighth-floor dining and fitness level. Renovations were scheduled to commence in July 2026 and conclude in December 2026. 

After raising approximately $40,000,000 in bonds, the buyer obtained a $128,461,693 loan from Hudson Bay Capital for the acquisition and is in the process of renaming the property The Arno.

The information in this comparable has been provided by sources deemed reliable.

Two industrial warehouse buildings totaling approximately 19,195 square feet sold on May 12, 2026, for $4,700,000. The Finger Companies and a private individual sold this 154-unit, 189,000 SF multifamily property to Duchesne Academy of the Sacred Heart for an undisclosed price. 

The buyer — a private all-girls Pre-K–12 school located directly east of the property — acquired the 7.94-acre parcel as part of its long-term campus expansion plan. 

The buyer's motivation was to secure adjacent land for future mission-driven planning under its capital campaign. The 1968-vintage, three-story masonry complex included a unit mix of 59 one-bedroom, 93 two-bedroom, and two three-bedroom residences on a 7.94-acre site.

The Westmoreland Apartments at 500 S Westmoreland Ave in Los Angeles, CA, sold on May 20, 2026, for $6,700,000, or approximately $124,074 per unit, based on 54 units. The four-story, 46,144-square-foot multifamily property was originally built in 1926 and underwent renovation in 1997. The sale reflects an investment transaction at a reported cap rate of 8.0%, indicating an estimated NOI of about $536,000. The site spans 0.33 acres and carries a building class C designation. The buyer was Spring Property Group, and the seller was Mosser through 500 S. Westmoreland Ave Associates, LP. At the time of sale, the property offered a mix of studio, one-bedroom, and two-bedroom units. The property was on the market for approximately 167 days with an initial asking price of $8,000,000. The information in this comparable has been verified by the listing broker and the buyer.

Tenant Managers sold a 140,392 SF office building in Houston’s Westchase submarket to Microvast Inc. for an undisclosed price. At the time of sale, the property was 89.2% occupied, with the remaining tenant’s lease nearing expiration, effectively positioning the asset as a near-vacant building. 

The seller had completed several capital improvements, resulting in a fully updated property at disposition.

The transaction was structured as an owner/user acquisition, with Microvast intending to relocate its headquarters to the property and bring approximately 100 employees to the location. This move is expected to provide increased activity within the surrounding Westchase area, with nearby hospitality assets, including a Marriott hotel located across the street, likely benefiting from the added demand.

This sale reflects a broader trend toward owner/user office acquisitions in the Houston market, as end users seek increased control over and customization of their office environments. 

Information in this comparable was verified by sources deemed reliable.

A private investor sold this 197-room, 92,825-SF hotel to MSH Holdings for $4,042,750, or approximately $20,522 per room and $43.55 per SF. 

The transaction was an auction sale carried out under distressed conditions, with significant deferred maintenance affecting pricing. 

The asset was marketed for roughly 111 days and offered fully unencumbered on a fee simple basis, free of existing debt and franchise obligations. The property was previously encumbered by a ground lease from the previous seller.  The ground lease was collapsed prior to the sale, enabling the property to trade fee simple.  The three-story building was constructed in 1972 and last renovated in 2013. 

Having operated under a national flag for many years, the hotel converted to independent branding in March 2025, positioning it as a value-add repositioning opportunity for new ownership.

Kidder Mathews Arranges $7.6 Million Sale of 36-Unit Carlton Apartments in Hollywood

Los Angeles, Calif. (June 16, 2026) – Kidder Mathews has successfully arranged the $7.6 million sale of The Carlton Apartments, a 36-unit property located at 5535 Carlton Way in Hollywood.

Kidder Mathews Executive Vice President Darin Beebower and Associate Dakoda Iversen represented Los Angeles-based James Investment Partners in the sale to a local real estate investor.

The property generated more than 25 offers from prospective buyers despite softening rental trends in parts of the Hollywood market, which have led many investors to more closely scrutinize underwriting assumptions and future rent growth projections.

“This transaction is a good example of the importance of persistence,” said Beebower. “We remained committed to the process, stayed engaged with the market, and were ultimately able to identify the right buyer to help our client achieve a successful sale.”

About Kidder Mathews
Kidder Mathews is the largest fully independent commercial real estate firm in the Western U.S., with over 900 professionals in 19 offices across Washington, Oregon, California, Nevada, and Arizona. We offer a complete range of brokerage, appraisal, asset services, consulting, and debt & equity finance services for all property types. Kidder Mathews averages $9 billion in transaction volume, manages 54 million square feet of space, and conducts nearly 2,700 appraisal, consulting, and cost segregation assignments annually. For more information, visit kidder.com.

American Landmark sold the 246-unit multifamily property known as The Henry at New Forest to Momentum Multifamily on September 29, 2025. 

The sale price was not disclosed.

Built in 2018, The Henry at New Forest is a four-story, 225,124-square-foot Class B, wood-frame apartment community situated on 10.2 acres at 14580 Crosby Freeway in Houston, Texas.

 The unit mix consists of 163 one-bedroom/one-bath units, one one-bedroom/one-and-a-half-bath unit, and 82 two-bedroom/two-bath units, with floor plans ranging from 634 to 1,274 square feet. Community amenities include a resort-style swimming pool, outdoor summer kitchens, fitness center, game lounge, professionally maintained dog park, and a Starbucks coffee café.


The recorded seller was Haven at Liberty Hills, LP, an affiliate of Tampa-based American Landmark Apartments. The recorded buyer was MP New Forest SPE LLC, an affiliate of Fort Worth-based Momentum Multifamily led by Dustin Miles. 

The disposition was consistent with American Landmark's active portfolio recycling program tied to the concurrent capital raise for its value-add-focused Fund V.
The buyer has publicly announced a value-add repositioning plan for the property, with pre-construction complete and scope including exterior paint, amenity upgrades, and a full leasing office refresh. The property continues to be managed by Asset Living post-close.

Invesco Ltd. sold the 1,452,818-square-foot, 64-story Class A office tower, one of Houston’s most recognizable office properties, to The Williams Companies, Inc. for $300,000,000, or approximately $206.50 per square foot. 

The transaction was structured as a purchase by the existing tenant, with Williams acquiring the namesake tower it had long occupied as part of its long-term growth strategy in the Houston market. At the time of sale, the property was approximately 85% occupied, and Williams will occupy approximately 360,000 square feet of the building as its Houston headquarters. 

The property features a conference center, multiple dining venues, and a fully staffed fitness facility, while also offering convenient access to numerous retail and restaurant destinations in the surrounding area. Long recognized as a defining element of the Houston skyline, the tower is home to several prominent tenants. The sale also included the adjacent parking garage.  

Invesco had owned the asset since 2013, when it acquired the property for $412,000,000. 

Originally constructed in 1983, the building underwent renovations completed in December 2020.

Camden Property Trust sold this 3,620-unit, 11-community apartment portfolio to CalSTRS for $1,625,000,000, or approximately $448,895 per unit. The acquisition was completed through a BlackRock-managed investment vehicle, with CalSTRS identified as the beneficial owner through the underlying entity and financing documentation.

The seller was motivated to divest as part of a full exit from California, citing regulatory operating costs equal to roughly 80 basis points of annual net operating income, and redeployed proceeds into debt repayment, share repurchases and 1031 exchange acquisitions in Sun Belt markets. 

Trailing 12-month occupancy across the portfolio averaged 96 percent at the time of sale. Assets were built between 2001 and 2021, with one community renovated in 2016. One community includes 38,970 square feet of ground-floor retail anchored by a health club, providing an additional income stream. 

Transaction costs totaled approximately $15,000,000, more than half attributable to a municipal transfer tax on a single asset.

Community amenities include a swimming pool, fitness center, business center, two laundry rooms, gated controlled access with perimeter fencing, assigned and reserved parking at $45 per month, courtyard, picnic area, and private lake access with a fishing pier.

 Situated across roughly 24.37 acres, the buildings were constructed between 1980 and 1984 and are single-storey masonry construction with diverse suite configurations serving a mix of tenants across various industries. At the time of marketing, the portfolio was 100 percent leased with approximately 3.1 years of weighted average lease term remaining, and its position along Beltway 8 offers direct connectivity to Interstate 45, Hardy Toll Road and Highway 59.

This transfer represents AvalonBay's residual portfolio consolidating into a merger of equals between AvalonBay Communities, Inc. and Equity Residential, who have collectively rebranded as Vivmark Residential.

The transaction was structured as an all-stock deal in which entity and membership interests transferred, and business value was included, with each AvalonBay shareholder receiving 2.793 Equity Residential shares. Following the completion of the merger, Vivmark Residential will trade on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker symbol “VMRK” beginning at the open of trading on August 18, 2026.

This 328-asset portfolio included 98,724 apartment units across 302 multifamily communities plus 15 retail assets, two office buildings and nine land parcels. Assets are located across 12 states and the District of Columbia, with the largest concentrations in California, Massachusetts, New Jersey and New York, and were an average of 95% leased at the time of sale.

Stephen Sterrett, Vivmark’s Chairman commented in a press release that "Vivmark represents a transformational opportunity to redefine the rental housing industry, utilizing our scale and capabilities to deliver superior value for shareholders.”

Information on this transaction was verified with the parties involved via press release.

A private investor sold this 25-unit apartment building to a private investor for $4,500,000, or $180,000 per unit ($268.88 per SF). The two-story, wood-frame mid-century building was constructed in 1956 and contains 16,736 SF on a 0.346-acre corner double lot, configured as nine studio units and sixteen one-bedroom/one-bathroom units. Thirteen units had been renovated prior to sale with new flooring, upgraded kitchens and bathrooms, and contemporary finishes, achieving market-leading rents, while the remaining twelve units were marketed with over 30% rental upside through a renovation and turnover strategy. Major capital improvements completed prior to sale included plumbing, electrical and window replacements, split-system air conditioning, and a seismic retrofit. The building offers approximately 24 on-site parking spaces and is separately metered for gas and electric, with master-metered water and sewer. It was on the market for 455 days, with an initial asking price of $4,795,000, and traded below asking. The in-place net operating income was reported to be $263,700, yielding an actual cap rate of 5.86%. The information in the comparable has been verified by the listing broker.

Sares-Regis Group sold a 169-unit apartment complex to Pacific Urban Investors, LLC for $70.49 million, or $417,101 per unit. According to CoStar data, the property was 96% occupied at the time of sale. 

Research verified the information in this comparable with sources deemed reliable.

A private individual sold this 303-unit multifamily property to Welltower Inc. for an undisclosed price on 7/31/26.

The information in this comparable has been verified through sources deemed reliable.

Florida Capital Real Estate Group sold this 292-unit apartment complex to American Landmark for an undisclosed price. 

The asset, formerly known as Park Avenue at Boulder Creek has been rebranded to Toscana Parkway. 

The three-story masonry complex sits on 16.81 acres, was completed in 2008 and offers a unit mix of 116 one-bedroom, 36 two-bedroom/one-bath, 110 two-bedroom/two-bath and 30 three-bedroom homes. The asset had not undergone a major capital renovation since original construction. 

The buyer cited limited new deliveries in the surrounding area, regional population growth and highway connectivity to major employment centers among its acquisition motivations. The buyer intends to execute the first capital improvement program since the community was built as part of a value-add strategy. 

Financing recorded in connection with the transaction totaled $31.29 million. 

The information in the comparable has been sourced from public record and verified by sources deemed reliable.

Brazos Residential acquired the 80 unit Woodway Garden from Cube Equity Group for an undisclosed price, according to public record. 

Woodway Garden Townhomes offers one-, two-, and three-bedroom flat, townhome, and loft-style homes ranging from 625 to 1,750 square feet, with select homes featuring private garages, fireplaces, vaulted ceilings, granite countertops, and study or den spaces. The buyer is planning an extensive renovation program to enhance property and better position it within the submarket. Enterprise Bank & Trust provided $11,138,575 in financing toward the trade. 

The details of this transaction derived from public record and the attached press release.
This is the result of inter-related parties.

A private individual sold this 8-unit, 7,212 SF apartment building to another private individual for an approximate  price of$4,299,090. The two-story, wood-frame multifamily asset was built in 1962 and was marketed as a stabilized investment. The property was on the market for approximately 220 days, with an initial asking price of $4,100,000, or $512,500 per unit, reflecting a gross rent multiplier of 12.25. Six of the eight units were fully renovated in 2022 and 2023, with a seventh renovated in 2025, leaving one unit remaining to be upgraded. Improvements included new unit interiors as well as upgraded plumbing, electrical, and cable/internet infrastructure, along with redone landscaping. The information in the comparable has been verified by the listing broker.

A private individual sold this 14,141-square-foot, two-storey office building to a private individual for an undisclosed price. Built in 1983 of masonry construction on a 1.01-acre site, the multi-tenant, second-generation asset was marketed for 707 days, with an initial asking price of $1,750,000, or approximately $123.75 per square foot. Improvements completed prior to sale include a roof installed in 2018 under a 10-year warranty and four rooftop HVAC units installed in 2008 and 2018. The interior build-out comprises 25 private offices, conference facilities, three reception areas, four restrooms with showers, and a previously built-out gym, supported by 52 surface parking spaces. The buyer financed the acquisition with a $1,300,000 loan. The information in the comparable has been verified by sources deemed reliable.

CIM Group, LP sold this 175-unit, 203,200-square-foot apartment building to Carmel Partners for an undisclosed price. Completed in 2016, the 11-story steel high-rise sits on 1.35 acres and includes a unit mix of 41 studios, 76 one-bedroom units and 58 two-bedroom units, with four levels of subterranean parking serving 472 vehicles. The buyer acquired the asset under a renovation strategy and has retained it as a held investment. Neither an asking price nor a marketing period was reported for the transaction, and no net operating income or cap rate was disclosed at the time of sale. The information in the comparable has been sourced from public record.

Grandview Partners sold a 26-unit apartment building to Category Company for $12,000,000, or $461,538 per unit. Completed in 2024, the purpose-built co-living asset contains 132 total suites across 44,872 square feet and was delivered vacant at the time of sale, offering an immediate lease-up opportunity. The building was on the market for 132 days, and an initial asking price was not disclosed. The asset is exempt from the Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance and features large-format four-, five-, and six-bedroom residences with a 1:1 bedroom-to-bathroom ratio. Amenities include a fitness center, rooftop lounge with firepit, courtyard, recreation room, and concierge, and residences are leased fully furnished with a per-resident utility bundle averaging $100 per month. Net operating income and cap rate were not reported at the time of sale. The information in the comparable has been verified by the buyer.

LaSalle Investment Management recapitalized an equity stake in CityWest, a four-building, approximately 1.5 million-square-foot office campus located at 2101-2107 CityWest Boulevard in West Houston, Texas, through a joint venture with private real estate investment firm 3Edgewood. 

Situated on approximately 39 acres near the intersection of Interstate 10 and Beltway 8, the property serves as a corporate headquarters-style campus and was reported to be 98% leased at the time of the transaction, supported by a long-duration tenant roster. 

The campus includes a recently renovated fitness center, basketball court and recreational facilities, multiple dining options, outdoor gathering areas, onsite services, and a secured, controlled-access environment designed to support tenant retention. 

According to LaSalle, CityWest has completed approximately 460,000 square feet of leasing activity since 2023 and has benefited from strong occupancy and leasing momentum within the West Houston office market. 

Transaction pricing and the size of the recapitalized equity interest were not disclosed.

Greystar Real Estate Partners sold this 378-unit apartment community to Turner Impact Capital for an undisclosed price. The property was encumbered by a ground lease at the time of sale, structured under a Texas public facility corporation that holds title to the land and leases it to the operator in exchange for an ad valorem tax exemption, with units reserved at 60% and 80% of area median income. 

Completed in 2023, the three-story community offers one- and two-bedroom floor plans ranging from 768 to 1,064 square feet, with in-unit washers and dryers, granite countertops, stainless steel appliances and keyless entry. Shared amenities include a resort-style pool, fitness centre, resident lounge, game room, dog park and detached garages. Electricity, water and trash are billed separately and are not included in residents' rent. 

Following completion, the developer stabilized the property more quickly than anticipated. During the initial marketing phase, a significant number of lease expirations coincided, resulting in elevated resident move-outs and a temporary decline in occupancy into the 80% range, which initially impacted buyer interest and pricing expectations. Occupancy recovered and the property was stabilized prior to closing, mitigating the vacancy concerns. 

The information in the comparable has been verified by sources deemed reliable.

A private entity sold this 28-unit apartment building to another private entity for $6,325,000, or $225,893 per unit. The two-story, 19,665-square-foot wood-frame building was constructed in 1964 and renovated in 2018, and sits on 0.46 acres with a unit mix of six studios, 17 one-bedroom units and five two-bedroom units. The asset was on the market for 181 days, with an initial asking price of $6,800,000. The in-place net operating income at the time of sale was reported to be $448,441, yielding an actual cap rate of 7.09%, with a gross rent multiplier of 8.33. The acquisition was completed with a recorded loan of $4,740,000. The information in the comparable has been verified by the listing broker.

On August 27th, 2026 a private entity sold this 24-unit apartment building to a private individual for $6,215,000, or $258,958 per unit. The sale was part of a 1031 exchange. The asset was on the market for 198 days, with an initial asking price of $6,800,000. Built in 1989, the building is exempt from the Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance. Most units were renovated prior to sale with stainless steel appliances, quartz countertops, upgraded cabinetry, vinyl plank flooring and central air conditioning, while second-floor units feature vaulted ceilings and private balconies. Gated ground-level parking provides 14 single and 12 tandem spaces, and a community laundry room with two washers and two dryers offers additional income. The in-place net operating income at the time of sale was reported to be $395,080, yielding a cap rate of 6.56%. The information in the comparable has been verified by the listing broker.

Gupta Houston TX Properties sold this 268,855-square-foot, nine-building flex-industrial park to a Private Investor for an undisclosed price. 

The single-story masonry and metal buildings were constructed between 1999 and 2004 and sit on 11.49 acres. 

The transaction was structured as a triple net investment sale. 

The asset was on the market for 126 days, with an initial asking price of $27,000,000. Suites offer private entrances, office and showroom areas, 12-by-12-foot front-loading grade-level roll-up doors, 20-foot clear heights, and insulated warehouse space, with no dock-high loading and 220-volt three-phase power. Small-bay spaces of 2,400 to 17,005 square feet were being marketed at $11.50 to $12.00 per square foot annually at the time of sale. 

The information in the comparable has been verified by sources deemed reliable.

On August 20th, 2026, Dominium sold this 216-unit, 204,667-square-foot apartment community to Pro Residential Services, Inc. for an undisclosed price. 

Built in 1996, the three-story wood-frame asset sits on 8.61 acres.

The unit mix comprises 70 one-bedroom, 78 two-bedroom and 68 three-bedroom homes. Amenities include a clubhouse, fitness center, swimming pool, sundeck, playground, controlled access, garage parking and in-unit washers and dryers.

 In connection with the transaction, the buyer secured a $9,685,000 loan from East West Bank.

The information in the comparable has been sourced from public record.
This was a non-market transaction and should not be used for sale comparable purposes.
This transaction is not a valid market sales transaction.  This was a change in title vesting as well as a refinance between inter-related parties and is therefore not valid for comparable purposes.

CoFe Properties sold these two flex buildings totaling 71,600 SF to a private entity for an undisclosed price on 8/24/26.

The information in this comparable has been verified through sources deemed reliable.

A private individual sold this 52,540 SF warehouse to Decker Capital for an undisclosed price. The single-story industrial building was constructed in 1984 and sits on 1.21 acres. As the sale price was undisclosed, net operating income and a corresponding cap rate cannot be derived. The information in the comparable has been sourced from public record.

Private Individual sold this 6,014-SF storefront retail/residential building to Private Individual for $1,600,000, or $266.04 per SF. The three-story masonry structure was built in 1949 and occupies a 1,695-SF lot on a pedestrian retail corridor zoned C2. The buyer acquired the building for owner-occupancy by a Los Angeles creative studio engaged in printing, fabrication, and installation of experiential works. Fong's Oriental Works of Art, an antique and gift shop operating at the site since 1952, previously occupied the ground floor and vacated in April 2014. The building had most recently been marketed as 100% leased with multiple tenancy, and was last conveyed in January 2025 for $1,550,000. The acquisition was financed with a $1,200,000 loan. The information in the comparable has been sourced from public record.

Realty Center Management, Inc. sold this 164-unit, two-building apartment portfolio to Fat Property for an undisclosed price. 

The transaction was negotiated off market, without a public listing or marketing campaign, so no asking price or days-on-market figure was established. 

The two mid-century communities, completed in 1962 and 1963, comprise a 66-unit two-story walk-up of efficiency and one-bedroom homes alongside a 98-unit, 11-story loft tower offering studio, one- and two-bedroom residences and penthouse lofts. Shared amenities include swimming pools, fitness centers, garage parking, controlled access, a rooftop patio and pet-friendly living. 

Financing of $9,000,000 was recorded in connection with the acquisition. 

The information in the comparable has been sourced from public record and verified by sources deemed reliable.

A private investor sold this 121-unit apartment community to Everflow Capital for an undisclosed price. Built in 1983 and renovated in 2008, the three-story, wood-frame complex spans 94,482 square feet across 4.02 acres, with an average unit size of 769 square feet. The unit mix consists of 84 one-bedroom/one-bath, 18 two-bedroom/one-bath, 17 two-bedroom/two-bath, and two three-bedroom/two-bath units. Average market rent at the time of sale was $1,044 per unit, or $1.36 per square foot, and the asset was offered as a full value-add opportunity across all units. Financing of $5,940,000 was recorded in connection with the transaction. Because the price was undisclosed, net operating income and a cap rate cannot be derived. The information in the comparable has been sourced from public record.

Houston Income Properties, Inc. sold this 389-unit garden-style apartment community to Indus Communities for an undisclosed price. 

The 1983-built asset was offered on an all-cash basis, with the buyer responsible for securing new financing, and was on the market for approximately 121 days without a published asking price.

 The community underwent a significant renovation in 2018, and the seller invested over $1.5 million in capital expenditures between January 2023 and December 2025, including roof replacements on 12 of the 34 buildings within the prior five years. A racquetball building was being converted into six additional units ahead of closing. A

t the time of sale, residents were billed separately for water and sewage, gas, trash and pest control. The site is located within a designated Opportunity Zone. 

The information in the comparable has been verified by sources deemed reliable.

A private individual sold this 4,216-square-foot, single-tenant warehouse building for $850,000, or $201.61 per square foot, in a transaction carrying a distress sale condition. The asset was marketed for 58 days with an initial asking price of $950,000, closing approximately 10.5% below ask. Built in 1981 on 0.146 acres and fully leased at the time of sale, the single-story reinforced concrete building offers 14-foot clear height, two grade-level drive-in doors, and 200-amp, 120/240-volt, three-phase, four-wire power, with fenced and gated surface parking (listing detail). Marketing materials offered an optional seller lease-back running from close of escrow through 31 December 2028 at $5,500 per month, with a one-time 3% increase to $5,665 effective 1 January 2027 (listing detail). Net operating income and cap rate were not reported. The information in the comparable has been sourced from public record.
This was a non-market transaction and should not be used for sale comparable purposes.

Cityview recapitalized its position in a 243-unit apartment complex for a recorded price of $76,045,000, or $312,942 per unit. LACERA exited the property and PCCP formed a JV with Cityview with $21.7 million in equity. 

The property was 90% occupied at the time of sale, and the cap rate for the transactions was 5.5%. 

Additionally, there was $52.35 million in financing associated with the recapitalization. 

Research verified the information in this comparable with sources deemed reliable.

Amgor Realty Inc sold a 0.66-acre development lot to A.F. Gilmore Company for $7,210,000, or approximately $10,924,086 per acre, equating to roughly $251 per land SF. 

The transaction closed at auction, drawing nine registered qualified bidders. The lot was on the market 74 days, following earlier campaigns asking $24,000,000 and later $13,700,000. 

The buyer already owned the adjoining 15,000-square-foot parking lot. The site was previously home to a theatre constructed in 1930. Demolition of the theatre, except for a portion of its facade, took place in 2023. The facade is required to remain. 

RTI plans approved in March 2024 permit a five-story, 71-unit mixed-use project above approximately 10,000 square feet of retail with five subterranean parking levels; subsequent zoning changes support alternatives of up to 146 residential units, or 96 hotel rooms with 90 residential units, subject to approvals.  As of the time of writing, the buyer was weighing their options and consulting architects about the future development.

The information in the comparable has been verified by sources deemed reliable. 

The transaction took place on the Ten-X auction platform.

TruePoint Capital LLC and Diversified Metroplex Investors sold this 608-unit apartment community to IDM Investments. The property sold for an undisclosed price. 

Built in 1972 and renovated in 1999, the two-storey, wood-frame community spans 280,727 square feet across 11.25 acres and comprises 192 one-bedroom/one-bath, 288 two-bedroom/one-bath, 64 two-bedroom/two-bath and 64 three-bedroom/two-bath units. The property was 52% occupied at sale and in disrepair. 

A loan of $17,406,000 was recorded in connection with the transaction. 

Amenities include a swimming pool, playground, controlled gated access, on-site maintenance and laundry facilities, with granite countertops and double-pane windows in the units. 

The information in the comparable has been sourced from public record.

Rivendell Global Real Estate, Inc. sold this 36-unit apartment property for $7,350,000, or $204,167 per unit. The buyer was not disclosed. The transaction was a standard investment sale, with no reported distress or unusual conditions. The property was on the market for 160 days, with an initial asking price of $8,500,000, and traded at a gross rent multiplier of 10.66. Ownership completed approximately $2 million in renovations and capital improvements over the five years preceding the sale, including remodeled interiors in 32 of the 36 units featuring hardwood flooring, soft-close cabinetry with stone countertops and stainless-steel appliances. Building systems were upgraded, covering the house electric system and electric sub-meters, modernized plumbing and electrical, and dual-pane windows. A new laundry room and common-area seating were also added.  The information in the comparable has been verified by the listing broker and the buyer broker.

Private Investor sold this 14-unit, 18,057-square-foot apartment community to a private investor for $5,390,000, or $385,000 per unit and $298.50 per square foot, at a gross rent multiplier of 11.01. Built in 1991 of reinforced concrete, the three-story building occupies a 0.25-acre (10,934-square-foot) lot zoned R3-1. The unit mix comprises eight two-story two-bedroom/two-and-a-half-bath townhome-style residences, five two-bedroom/two-bath units and one studio, with the two-bedroom plans measuring approximately 1,100 square feet each. Select units offer fireplaces, private balconies, dishwashers, granite countertops, stainless steel appliances, hardwood floors, walk-in closets, central air and security systems; shared improvements include gated subterranean parking with 25 spaces and on-site laundry. Constructed after 1978, the asset falls outside Los Angeles rent stabilization and is governed by AB 1482. It was on the market for 58 days, with an initial asking price of $5,375,000, and closed $15,000 above the asking price. The seller had acquired the property in November 1993 for $1,285,000. The information in the comparable has been verified by the listing broker and the buyer.

U.S. Capital Investment LLC sold this 18,852 SF retail building to Alym Lakhani for an undisclosed price on 12/29/23.

The information in this comparable was verified through sources deemed reliable.

On September 28, 2026, American Landmark sold this 234-unit, 250,848 SF multifamily community to Expedition Capital Advisors for an undisclosed price. 

Built in 2007 on 10.038 acres, the two-story, wood-frame garden-style asset comprises 92 one-bedroom, 132 two-bedroom and 10 three-bedroom units. Amenities include attached and detached garages, a private community fishing lake and a resort-inspired pool. 

The seller acquired the community in 2019, renamed it from Newport on the Lake and announced a $5.9 million capital improvement program shared with another Houston asset. 

The acquisition aligns with the buyer's strategy of acquiring conventional market-rate multifamily assets in high-growth markets. 

Acquisition financing of $24,407,000 was recorded. 

The information in the comparable has been sourced from public record.
This was a Trustees Deed upon Sale and therefore should not be used for comparable purposes.

The reported transfer reflects an internal restructuring among entities under common ownership. The buyer and seller are interrelated parties, and the conveyance was executed for organizational and accounting purposes rather than open-market exposure. 

The asset was not formally marketed, and pricing is considered non-indicative of prevailing market conditions. As such, this transaction should be treated as a non-market sale and excluded from direct market-based pricing analysis.

On October 8, 2026, a private investor sold this 84,000-SF, six-story office building to Hays Electrical Services for an undisclosed price. The buyer plans to demolish this building at some point in the future. The reinforced concrete structure was built in 1984, renovated in 2021 and sits on 4.48 acres. It has access to Beltway 8, Interstate 45 and the Hardy Toll Road, near George Bush Intercontinental Airport. The information in the comparable has been verified by sources deemed reliable,
